News.title: Man, 56, attacked inside home dies two days after ‘refusing medical care’ – as two men arrested over ‘murder’
News.content:
MURDER PROBE Man, 56, attacked inside home dies two days after ‘refusing medical care’ – as two men arrested over ‘murder’

TWO men have been arrested on suspicion of murder after a 56-year-old man who “refused medical care” died following an alleged assault.

Brian Cunliffe died after the reported attack in Wigan, Greater Manchester, on Friday, cops said.

Cops and emergency services scrambled to Bryn Street just after 10.30pm after ambulance services reported an “ongoing disturbance” in which a man “had blood coming from his face”.

A man in his 50s and a man in his 30s were arrested and remain in police custody as the investigation continues.





The arrested men and the victim are believed to be known to each other, Grater Manchester Police said.

Cunliffe initially refused medical care on Friday saying “he did not remember how he got his injuries”, said the force.

He told cops he “would take himself to the hospital in the morning”.

Police were later alerted by Salford Royal Hospital that the victim was in a life-threatening condition at about 12 noon on Saturday.

Cunliffe then passed away on Sunday, two days after the initial “disturbance”.

Cops said that his grieving family are being supported and fully updated throughout.

Detective Inspector Hulston, of GMP’s Major Incident Team (MIT), said: “I would like to express my deepest condolences to the family of the deceased during this incredibly difficult time.

“Our Family Liaison Officers are supporting the family of the deceased, and we are ensuring they are fully updated throughout.



“We are continuing to establish the full facts of this incident, but we believe both suspects and the victim were known to each other.

“I would like to reassure the community in Wigan that this is an isolated incident.

“We have two men in custody who are currently being questioned by my officers, we will provide further updates when we know more.”

News.title: Girl, 9, was camping in Scots industrial estate with family before death as man ‘known to her’ arrested
News.content:
COPS have issued an update on the suspicious death of a nine-year-old girl in Arbroath.

The child died at Ninewells Hospital in Dundee after being found seriously hurt on the Elliot Industrial Estate.

Detectives have said a 35-year-old white British man was arrested in connection with her death.

They confirmed the girl and the man are known to each other and were part of a family from West Yorkshire who were camping in the area.





Detective Inspector Mike Ness of the Major Investigation Team said: “Our thoughts remain with those affected by these events.

“Members of the public will see an increased police presence and activity in the area as enquiries continue.

“This is intended to reassure the public and anyone who may have information should approach these officers or contact Police Scotland on 101, quoting incident number 0008 of Monday, 3 August 2026.”

Eyewitnesses say they saw a campsite set up on the industrial estate.



Karen Youngson was picking up a friend from the gym when she passed the scene.

She told the BBC: “When I first went up there, I was like my goodness why is there a tent there?

“There were two camping chairs, that’s all I saw, but it was the amount of rubbish, it was unbelievable.

“It was dark, there was no noise coming from the place, it wasn’t like there were lights or anyone sitting outside.”



A police spokesperson added: “Extensive enquiries are ongoing after a nine-year-old girl was found seriously injured in Elliot Industrial Estate in Arbroath around 12.02am on Monday, 3 August 2026.

“She was taken to Ninewells Hospital in Dundee, where she later died.

“Her death is being treated as suspicious, and a 35-year-old white British man has been arrested. The nine-year-old girl and the 35-year-old man are known to each.

“Officers are not looking for anyone else in connection with her death and the other members of the family, from West Yorkshire, who were camping in the area, are being supported by specialist officers.”

More to follow…

News.title: Can I leave my bins out while I’m on holiday? Your legal rights explained
News.content:
WITH August officially here, Brits will be heading off on holiday for some much needed relaxation.

However, amidst the packing rush, many may forget to move their wheelie bin – an issue that can unexpectedly land you with a hefty fine.

Leaving bins out for collection when heading on holiday, even with good intentions, gives the council the right to send a written warning, or issue a large fine.



This is down to a rather unknown law that can penalise Brits for putting out their bins incorrectly.



Under the Environmental Protection Act, local councils have the power to hit you with a penalty if your bin becomes a nuisance to neighbours.

This can be for a number of reasons, including putting waste out that causes an obstruction to neighbours, forcing people using wheelchairs or buggies to walk onto the road.

It can also be issued if your waste bin looks “unsightly”, such as bags being torn and wheelie bins being turned over.



Two specified rules, however, directly target Brits leaving their bins out for a long period of time, such as to go on holiday.

Fines can be issued if the bin restricts access to pavements and streets, caused by leaving any waste receptacle out for several days.

It also includes if the bin is likely to attract vermin, such as foxes and rats, which also occurs when bags and bins are left for several days before waste collection.

If these rules are broken, the council can send you a warning, and even issue a Fixed Penalty Notice to your household, which is set at a maximum of £80.



To dodge the fine, get a friendly neighbour, relative, or friend to wheel your bin out on collection day when you go away, and take it back in once it is empty.

Before jetting off on holiday, it is important to check the exact date of your bin collection, leaving you enough time to make these arrangements and avoid an unnecessary £80 fine.

News.title: Can my neighbour sunbathe naked in their garden? Full laws and rules explained
News.content:
WITH the warm weather continuing this week, your neighbour might decide it’s the perfect opportunity to sunbathe in the nude.

But is it actually legal for your neighbour to bare all in the great outdoors?

According to the College of Policing’s guidance on public nudity, naturalism is a “belief in a natural, naked lifestyle” which falls under the right to freedom of expression.



As a result, your neighbour has every right to be naked in the privacy of their own garden – as much as you might not want to see it.



But this all changes if the intent behind their actions is to harm others.

Under the Sexual Offences Act 2003, public nudity becomes a crime if it involves “deliberately exposing genitalia towards another person with the intention of them seeing and being caused alarm or distress”.

Also known as indecent exposure, this is a crime that can carry a two year prison sentence, as well as an unlimited fine, community service and a mandatory placement on the Sex Offenders Register.



The Crown Prosecution Service adds that a “balance needs to be struck between the right to freedom of expression and the right of the wider public to be protected from harassment, alarm and distress”.

So if you believe that your neighbour is stripping down with the intention to hurt others, you do have a legal right to complain and get authorities involved.

But it is not a crime for them to simply bare all in the summer sun.

And if you are seeing a little too much of your neighbour lately;



A polite discussion and a suggestion to invest in some privacy fences can go a long way in reaching a happy compromise.

News.title: Chaos as TWO major UK motorways are forced to shut due to blazes – with one closed for 5 hours
News.content:
MOTOR MAYHEM Chaos as TWO major UK motorways are forced to shut due to blazes – with one closed for 5 hours

TWO major motorways have ground to a halt after a hay trailer burst into flames and a separate fire sparked on an embankment.

Plumes of smoke were seen off the M5 near Quinton, Birmingham, while traffic is also standstill on the M4 near Swindon, Wiltshire – and has been for FIVE hours.



National Highways says traffic is being held due to a fire which has spread onto the embankment at the edge of the M5 between junctions 3 and 4.

It said: “Traffic is currently being held on the M5 southbound between J3 (Quinton) and J4 (LydiateAsh) due to an off-network fire which has spread to the embankment.”



Hereford & Worcester fire crews are on the scene, with the statement adding at lunchtime: “Current delays of 10 mins and 2 miles of congestion on the approach.”

Meanwhile, emergency services rushed to the M4 westbound to battle the blaze this morning.



Traffic on all lanes between junction 15 and 16 was stopped after the fire erupted on the HGV’s trailer.

Dorset and Wiltshire Fire and Rescue Service said crews are on the scene dealing with the fire.

A spokesperson added: “The M4 is currently closed westbound between J15 and J16 while we deal with a fire involving a trailer of hay.”

Drivers have been warned of hour long delays as firefighters douse the burning trailer.



Wiltshire Police said: “Please be aware that the M4 westbound between junctions 15 and 16 is closed due to a significant lorry fire.

“Please find alternate routes. We will provide updates when appropriate.

“This is expected to be closed for around five hours.

“Please allow extra time for journeys.”

The AA‘s traffic monitors added: “All lanes stopped and queueing traffic due to vehicle fire on M4 Westbound between J15 A419 Marlborough Road (Swindon East) and J16 A3102 Swindon Road (Swindon West).”



National Highways said the fire has caused four miles of congestion and advises motorists to allow extra time.

A spokesperson added: “Delays of 60 minutes and approx. 4 miles of congestion on approach.

“Please allow extra time if you’re travelling in the area. More to follow.”

News.title: Two crypto millionaires kidnapped, tied up & stripped naked in blackmail plot after being targeted by ‘overseas kingpin’
News.content:
CRYPTO HOSTAGES Two crypto millionaires kidnapped, tied up & stripped naked in blackmail plot after being targeted by ‘overseas kingpin’

TWO cryptocurrency millionaires were kidnapped, tied up and forced to strip naked in a horrifying blackmail plot, a court heard.

The wealthy pair were said to have been targeted by an overseas kingpin, known as Nino, after flashing their luxurious lifestyle on social media.



Seven men accused of charges including kidnap, blackmail, sexual assault and false imprisonment appeared at Inner London Crown Court last week.

The court heard the victims had been taken while visiting London from France on the orders of Nino, real name Ibrahim Mohamed, last July.



Jurors were told Mohamed – who is still at large – had orchestrated the operation through social media sites WhatsApp and Snapchat.

Cops tracked down the missing victims and caught three members of the gang after a high-speed chase through the capital.



The millionaires, both aged in their 20s, had been staying in Kensington, West London, at the time of the horror.

Prosecuting, Heidi Stonecliffe KC said they may have attracted “unwanted attention” by posting about their extravagant lifestyles online.



They were ambushed and captured by three masked men armed with guns after travelling to the other side of London to buy cannabis.

Both men were forced back into their rented Mercedes, which was driven to a nearby flat.

The duo were then held in a tower block in Canning Town, East London, and ate just one KFC spicy chicken wing during their capture.

Jurors were told horrific details of their capture, such as having boiling water poured over their bodies.

Cigarettes were also stubbed out across their faces and in their mouths while they were cable tied and gagged during the “cold hard torture”.



Members of the gang threatened to cut their genitals off and rape one of their girlfriends.

One of the victims claimed he had even been made to drink toilet water during the terrifying 52-hour ordeal.

And they were forced to starve as the offenders scoffed the rest of the 20-piece bucket, the court heard.



The millionaires transferred the gang $30,000 in cryptocurrency, allowing one of them to be freed.

But the other victim feared he was being sold to another gang in a sick bid to extort more money from him.

The pair were eventually traced by the Met Police‘s Flying Squad and rescued by officers after a 70mph chase through residential streets.

Cops found one victim with his hands tied and burn marks all over his face.

They tracked down the gang’s hideout after a pal of the victims urged them to trace his phone, which had been left in their Mercedes.



Yasir Mohamed, 23, Julius George, 22, Isaac Bakoya, 18, Adel Sineen, 18, Gerson Borges, 24, Mohamed Osman, 29, and William Adebisi, 19, were all arrested by cops.

Lawyers for the defendants denied any kidnap attempt and claimed their clients had legitimately been getting the pair to pay up for the cannabis.

The court was also told that one of the victims was being probed for fraud in his home country.



Mohamed, of Forest Gate, East London was cleared of kidnap charges, false imprisonment, possessing an imitation firearm and sexual assault.

The jury also failed to reach a verdict on conspiracy to blackmail and the CPS is yet to decide whether he will be tried again over the charges.

Sineen, of Camberwell, South London, admitted dangerous driving but was cleared of false imprisonment and possessing a knife.

Borges, also of Camberwell, and Osman, of Finsbury Park, North London, were both found guilty of conspiracy to blackmail and false imprisonment.

Adebisi, of Romford, Essex, was also found guilty of false imprisonment.



George, of Earlsfield, South West London, was convicted of false imprisonment and admitted to carrying a knife.

Bakoya, of West Norwood, South London, admitted false imprisonment but was cleared of possessing a knife.

Allegations of sexual assault – made against two members of the gang – were cleared by the jury.

Osman, Adebisi, Borges, Bakoya, George and Sineen are all due to be sentenced next month.

Flying Squad Detective Chief Inspector Laura Hillier said: “These convictions demonstrate the Met’s determination to pursue those involved in serious violence, even in the most challenging circumstances.

“It sends a clear message that offenders cannot assume they can evade justice simply because victims are unable or unwilling to give evidence.

“This outcome reflects our continued commitment to tackling serious violence, protecting vulnerable people and keeping London safe.”

News.title: When will it rain in the UK? Latest Met Office weather forecast with thunderstorms to come this week
News.content:
THUNDERSTORMS are predicted to bring the first proper rain in weeks after the driest July in nearly 200 years.

It comes as the mercury is set to hit highs of 35C today, leaving parts of England hotter than Greece.



When will it rain in the UK?

According to the Met Office, it started raining in Scotland this morning.

Heavy rain north of the border is due to set in overnight and last through Tuesday morning.



This evening brings the first hints of rain in southern England, with isolated thunderstorms possible.

Elsewhere is forecast to stay cloudy with outbreaks of rain and a risk of thunder.



Tuesday sees heavy rain push into the North with a risk of thunder and windy conditions.

A yellow thunderstorm warning covers the whole of Northern Ireland from midday on Tuesday until 9pm.

So the heaviest rain is heading for Scotland and the North, while the drought-hit South is set to see some showers before turning drier again from Thursday.

The rain comes after the driest July since 1836, when King William IV was on the throne.



Reservoir levels have dropped sharply, eight water companies have brought in hosepipe bans, and half of England has now been declared in drought.

Tinder-dry ground also left fire crews stretched, with 208 wildfires tackled across England and Wales in under a fortnight last month.

Met Office scientist Dr Emily Carlisle said: “The headline story for July is undoubtedly the rainfall.

“Across parts of England and Wales, we’ve seen extraordinarily low totals, with some locations recording little or no meaningful rainfall for much of the month.

“Provisional figures suggest this could be one of the driest Julys in nearly two centuries of records.



“This is particularly notable when coupled with the exceptional heat experienced so far this summer.”

How hot will it be this week?

The Met Office has predicted soaring temperatures on Monday, followed by rain and a “gradual cooling down process”.

Met Office forecaster Marco Petagna said: “We’re going with a headline of 34C on Monday, but with a potential for local 35C in the South East, the Midlands into the low 30s as well.

“So central and southern England, widely high 20s to low 30s, and approaching or if not touching, the mid 30s in the South East.



“[Monday] is the peak of the heat – temperatures do come down a little bit, we’re still talking 28 to 30C on Tuesday.

“Again, the South East and East Anglia we’re seeing the highest temperatures on Tuesday, so not as extreme as tomorrow, but still well above average.”

He continued: “And then even by Wednesday, we’re looking at high 20s, 26 or 27C, in the South East.

“But it’s a gradual cooling down process through the week, and always cooler towards the North and West in any case, high teens, low 20s, but certainly central and South East England seeing hot weather returning briefly, and a lot of sunshine to come in the South East as well.”

The forecaster added that Wales is expected to reach the high 20s on Monday before cooling to the mid-20s in the following days.



Scotland avoids the scorching temperatures altogether, with highs of just 19C today – around 15C cooler than the South East.

Glasgow sees highs of 20C on Tuesday, before slipping back to 18C on Wednesday and Thursday, and 17C on Friday.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Amber heat health alerts have been issued from 9am on Monday morning for the East Midlands, East of England, South East and London.

The UK Health Security Agency has also issued a yellow alert for the North West, Yorkshire and The Humber, the West Midlands and the South West.

News.title: Man, 60, who kept his mum’s body in living room freezer for three years while pocketing £78k in benefits is jailed
News.content:
SICK SCHEME Man, 60, who kept his mum’s body in living room freezer for three years while pocketing £78k in benefits is jailed

A MAN who stashed his mum’s body in her freezer and left her there for years as he plundered her pension and benefits has been jailed.

Christopher Phillips admitted putting his mum’s body in a chest freezer at their home after she died in 2023.



He plundered the savings of retired company secretary Sylvia, 89, to fund his bachelor lifestyle in the seaside town of Porthcawl in Wales.

Former company director Phillips also failed to disclose to the department of work and pensions and Bridgend Council that his mum has died.



He continued to keep his mother’s body in the freezer for three years while receiving more than £78,000 in her benefits.

At Merthyr Tydfil Crown Court today, Judge Tracey Lloyd-Clarke sentenced Phillips to two years and four months’ imprisonment.

Phillips told doctors he “did not want to let her go” and “wanted more time” after her death on March 8, 2023.

Phillips, 60, had earlier admitted preventing the lawful and decent burial of a dead body and two counts of fraud.

He failed to notify the Department for Work and Pensions and Bridgend County Borough Council that his mother had died.

The court heard Phillips left work to become a full-time carer for his mother in the months leading up to her death.



Following her death, for which the cause remains unknown, the defendant purchased a chest freezer.

He then used this to store her body inside the living-room of their Porthcawl home.

Sylvia’s body was found by cops in February 2026 after a concern for welfare call from her GP.

The court heard the body was covered with a leopard print throw and found alongside roses.

It was also chillingly found alongside a birthday card, reading “To Mum, from Christopher and Tina”, a reference to the family dog.



Phillips received a total of £78,190.92 in benefits following his mother’s death.

The fiend “intending to make a gain” by keeping news of his mother’s death hidden, the court heard.

Representing Phillips, Ruth Smith told a previous hearing he had “lived on” money plundered from his mother’s account.

She said: “It is accepted that Mr Phillips did continue withdrawing the money from his mother’s account and effectively lived on that, which is supported by the analysis of his bank accounts.”

Phillips held his dead mother in his arms and told her he would look after her, the court was told.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Two days after her death, he then purchased the chest freezer from AO and put it in their semi-detached home.

Phillips constantly denied requests from her local GP surgery to contact Sylvia, the court heard.

News.title: Late Queen Elizabeth's 'horse whisperer' pal dies as his family pays emotional tribute
News.content:
Late Queen Elizabeth's 'horse whisperer' pal dies as his family pays emotional tribute

Monty Roberts, a celebrated horse trainer who struck up a close friendship with Queen Elizabeth II, has died at the age of 91, his family has announced

View 4 Images The late Queen and Queen Camilla with horse trainer Monty Roberts at the Royal Mews at Buckingham Palace in 2015 (Image: Getty Images)

A celebrated horse trainer dubbed the ‘horse whisperer’ who struck up an unlikely friendship with the late Queen has died, his family has announced.

‌



American Monty Roberts, who bonded with the former monarch over their shared love of the animals, died aged 91, with his family paying an emotional tribute to him on social media. Mr Roberts became revered around the world for his compassionate, non-violent approach to training animals. He earned the nickname the Real Horse Whisperer and is said to have inspired the Robert Redford movie and book of the same name.

‌



He first connected with Elizabeth II in 1989, when she had read with interest about his horse training approach, and eventually he was invited to Windsor Castle to meet her, the late Queen Mother and Prince Philip.

‌



Inside King Charles' tough challenge as pivotal royal aide to leave Palace after two decades READ MORE :

View 4 Images Mr Roberts has died at the age of 91 (Image: Getty Images)

What followed was a friendship between the pair, which spanned until the late Queen’s death in September 2022. His daughter Debbie wrote on Instagram: “It is with profound sadness that I share the passing of my father, Monty Roberts, on July 31, 2026.

“For the world, he was known as the man who listens to horses. To me, he was simply Dad, a man of extraordinary kindness, unwavering integrity, and an unshakable belief that trust could accomplish what force never could.

‌



“For more than eight decades, he dedicated his life to changing the way people understand and work with horses. His mission reached far beyond horsemanship.

“He believed that true leadership is built on communication, patience, empathy, and respect; lessons that have touched the lives of countless people around the world.”

View 4 Images The pair together in 1989

‌



In an interview with the Mirror after the late Queen’s death, Mr Roberts opened up about his friendship with her, which included long lunches with the monarch.

He said: “Our lunches together in her palaces were no longer pinch-me moments. I was part of her life, she was part of mine and I don’t think any one of us thought it was strange. My wife Pat and I stayed with her at Buckingham Palace for weeks at a time and she treated us like family.”

In 1996, he says he followed royal orders when the Queen told him: “There must be a book – you have to take your work to the world.” His autobiography, The Man Who Listens to Horses, sold in 41 countries was a best seller for 58 weeks. The Queen clearly appreciated his work, making him a member of the Royal Victorian Order for his services in 2011.

‌



View 4 Images Mr Roberts received his Royal Victorian Order in 2011

But he told the Mirror it was the small gestures of friendship which he treasured even more than the medals or gifts such as corkscrews saved from the Windsor Castle fire and a lead plaque stamped the royal crest.

He said at the time: “Can you believe the Queen always took my phone calls? Only once I was told she couldn’t speak to me because she was with Northern Ireland’s politicians. Right then I heard, ‘Monty! What are you doing? I’m out of my meeting to talk to you’. I just about fell off my chair.”

‌



Mr Roberts also recalled how he was, fittingly, in a pen with horses on his Santa Ynez Valley farm when he was told the news of the late Queen’s death. He said: “I was working with a very difficult horse. And I watched Pat and my daughter Debbie come together at the top of the fence looking sombre.

“I’d already heard the Queen was under constant care but said to myself, it’ll be OK – she’s gonna come through and she’ll be bouncing around again. “But when I finished working with that horse, they said, ‘Brace yourself. The Queen has died’.

Article continues below

“That moment will never be forgotten by this cowboy. A lot of important people are saying we have to let the Queen go. But I can’t let go.”

He added: “British people might find it hard to believe their Queen enjoyed being with a cowboy. But she did.”

News.title: Should King Charles join Prince Harry at the Invictus Games? Take our poll and have your say
News.content:
Should King Charles join Prince Harry at the Invictus Games? Take our poll and have your say

The Duke of Sussex has expressed his wish for the monarch to join him at the 2027 Invictus Games, which will take place in Birmingham, as the father and son continue to mend their relationship

View 4 Images Harry and Charles recently reunited in a private family meeting at Highgrove (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

Prince Harry has expressed his wishes for his father, King Charles, to join him at the 2027 Invictus Games, which will be held in Birmingham. It is believed that the organisers of the sporting event - which was founded by the Duke of Sussex to help injured veterans - are planning to invite the monarch to take part in either the opening or closing ceremony, while also hoping he will attend a range of the sporting events to meet competitors.

‌



It is understood that Harry will attend next year's Games, after he recently made a five-day trip to his home country to mark the official one year countdown to the 2027 event.

‌



Inside King Charles' tough challenge as pivotal royal aide to leave Palace after two decades READ MORE :

View 4 Images King Charles with his youngest son Prince Harry (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



While in the UK, Harry - along with his wife Meghan Markle and their children Archie and Lilibet - reunited with the King and Queen in Highgrove in a private meeting, marking the first time Charles had seen his grandchildren in several years.

Harry has been making steps to mend his relationship with his father, engaging in private meetings over the last few years, as they work towards a reconciliation.

The prince’s relationship with his father has been strained since he and Meghan quit their royal roles in 2020 and relocated to America, where the Duke and Duchess of Sussex did not shy away from speaking candidly about their experiences within the Firm.

‌



On several occasions, Harry and Meghan levelled public jibes at the Royal Family, most notably in their 2021 interview with Oprah Winfrey, their 2022 Netflix docuseries, and in Harry’s autobiography Spare, which was released in 2023.

However, as the King’s cancer diagnosis was made public in 2024, Harry expressed his wishes to rekindle a relationship with his estranged father. In September 2025, when Harry was in the UK for the annual WellChild Awards, he and the King had a private meeting at Clarence House, which was their first face-to-face meeting in 19 months.

‌



Now, Harry believes by having the King at the Invictus Games, it will continue to be a step in the right direction for them to patch up their relationship, while also giving more gravity to Harry’s fight for security when in his home country.

One insider said: “Harry’s intention is two fold. He would love the King’s support at the Games, while having his father by his side would also add considerable weight to his argument for security for his family to accompany him on the trip. “

Sources close to the duke also suggested his desire to have his father by his side at next year’s Invictus Games serves a dual purpose. Another source said: “Next year is a big deal for Harry. He is determined that the Birmingham Games will be the best ever and it would mean the world to him to have his father there." Another royal source suggested the King “would welcome the opportunity to see his grandchildren again”.

‌



View 4 Images Harry attended the one year countdown event in Birmingham last month (Image: Getty Images)

However, one royal expert believes that if the King is seen at the Invictus Games, it may upset the monarch’s eldest son, Prince William. Earlier this year, former BBC royal correspondent Jennie Bond told the Mirror that supporting Harry presents Charles with a dilemma, as he will be reluctant to be seen to be siding with one son over the other.

She explained: “Invictus has become pivotal. It is Harry’s great cause and his greatest achievement and any father would want to support his son as the games come to the UK. But it’s not straightforward for the King – sadly for him, his family matters never are.

‌



“It could become a classic case of a father having to choose between his warring sons. We can only imagine how William might feel if Charles publicly threw his support behind the games and Harry.

“William has bitten his lip, risen above the accusations and knuckled down to the job, in spite of the brutal cancer diagnoses for both Catherine and Charles. To see his father stand on a very public platform and salute Harry’s achievement would be tough. But that’s the dilemma the King might face.”

View 4 Images Charles attended the opening ceremony of the 2014 London Invictus Games (Image: Getty Images)

‌



In January, a spokesperson for Invictus said: a spokesman said: “The royal family have been longstanding supporters of the Invictus Games since its inception in 2014."

“While it is too early to confirm who will attend in 2027 as invitations have not yet been sent out, organisers of the Invictus Games Birmingham 2027 will issue invitations to members of the Royal Family in due course, and we would very much welcome their presence.”

Harry is continuing with planning for next year’s Invictus Games, which he originally launched in London in 2014, with the competition aiming to challenge "perceptions of disability, champion adaptive sport, and demonstrate the resilience, determination and unconquered spirit of wounded, injured and sick service personnel and veterans”.

Article continues below

It has since been held in Orlando, Toronto, Sydney, The Hague, Düsseldorf and Vancouver-Whistler, Canada for the inaugural winter games in 2025.

News.title: Nigel Farage – live: Reform UK leader panics after polls drop and opens door to Restore deal after Tice probed
News.content:
Nigel Farage will break cover to hold a press conference at 11am today - it will be the first one in London held by the Reform UK leader for months, and comes amid ongoing questions about his finances

Under-pressure Nigel Farage will break cover to hold a press conference at 11am today.

It will be the first London press conference held by the Reform UK leader for months. Mr Farage has been laying low since he last month dramatically quit as the MP for Clacton to trigger a by-election in the area.

This time last year, Reform UK was holding weekly press conferences over the summer. But in recent months, as pressure grows over Mr Farage's finances, the party has scurried away from scrutiny.

A standards investigation into Mr Farage's failure to declare a £5million gift from Thai-based cryptocurrency billionaire Christopher Harborne has been paused since he quit as an MP. It will be restarted if he is re-elected as an MP in next week's Clacton by-election.

Follow live updates below...

News.title: Ariana Grande leans on ex she 'really trusts' as she steps back from public life
News.content:
Ariana Grande leans on ex she 'really trusts' as she steps back from public life

Ariana Grande has told fans she is taking some time away after her tour after public scrutiny - but there's one familiar face she is seeking support from as she has a break

View 5 Images Ariana is set to take a step back from public life after her Eternal Sunshine tour (Image: Getty Images)

As Ariana Grande announces plans to step away from public life, the singer has been leaning on a familiar face for support.

‌



While she famously sang about her past relationships in her hit single Thank U, Next, the 33-year-old pop star remains on great terms with ex Ricky Alvarez, whom she recently started dating again. The announcement comes after Ariana revealed she is "taking a step back from visibility", explaining that recent public appearances had sadly led to "endless, ongoing public scrutiny".

‌



Last month, a source told People that Ariana and Ricky were " taking things very slowly”, adding: " She’s not held ill will against him [since their split]. Ricky is dependable, trustworthy and very supportive. Ariana feels she can be herself around Ricky.”

‌



While the singer hasn't explicitly linked her hiatus to discussions surrounding her health or appearance, body image comments from the public have intensified in recent months. A representative for Ariana said: "Ariana will be taking a step back from visibility after she completes the Eternal Sunshine Tour.

Jameela Jamil's Ariana Grande warning as Petals singer announces break READ MORE :

5 View 5 Images Ariana has announced she is taking some time away from the spotlight (Image: Getty Images for Ariana Grande) 5 View 5 Images She said the comments about her weight can be "uncomfortable" (Image: Corbis via Getty Images)

‌



"She looks forward to finishing the tour and ending it on a high note, both healthily and happily, and then taking a much-deserved break from public-facing work and appearances, which has led to endless, ongoing public scrutiny This tour has been a beautiful experience for her. She loves her fans and has loved every minute of this tour so much."

Helping her navigate this transition is her former backup dancer and current boyfriend Ricky Alvarez, whom she dated from 2015 to 2016. In 'Thank U, Next', Ariana originally sang: "Wrote some songs about Ricky / Now I listen and laugh."

Adding to the speculation around their rekindled romance, she recently tweaked the lyrics during a live performance to: "Wrote some songs about Ricky / I know he's still got my back" - and in another performance teased "Wrote some songs about Ricky / And they still kinda slap."

‌



Sources confirm that Ricky joined Ariana and her family for the 4th of July holiday in Florida, and that he's been a frequent presence on her current tour. A source told PEOPLE: "She's having a great time on tour. She loves having close friends join her for parts of the tour. Ricky has always been a friend and confidant. She really trusts him. He has such great, positive energy, makes her laugh and she enjoys spending time with him."

View 5 Images There have been ongoing speculations about the singers weight and health recently (Image: Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images)

Another source added: "Ariana has always considered Ricky a friend. She’s not held ill will against him. Ricky is dependable, trustworthy and very supportive.

‌



"Ariana feels she can be herself around Ricky. They have a similar, smart, dry sense of humour. They’re not jumping into anything serious right away, but Ari is happy to have him back in her life. Ricky has always been a friend and confidant. He has such great, positive energy, makes her laugh, and she enjoys spending time with him."

The pair were also spotted grabbing lunch together on June 26, ahead of her show in Austin, Texas.

This rekindling following Ariana's recent split from her Wicked co-star Ethan Slater after nearly three years together. Insiders note that she is "doing really well" post-breakup, adding: "Her relationship with Ethan is 100% over. She's focused on her tour and spending time with the people who have always been there for her."

‌



Ariana and Ricky originally broke up amicably due to the pressures of her career. Following their split, Ariana dated Mac Miller, Pete Davidson, Dalton Gomez, and Ethan Slater, but maintained a friendly connection with Ricky throughout.

When 'Thank U, Next' was first released in 2018, he posted a lighthearted video listening to his shoutout, captioning it: "Nothing but gratitude...Thank you, next… (those songs are fire tho… you're welcome)."

Ariana reshared it with a laugh, writing : " HAHAHAHAHHAHAHAH IM SORRY U GOT THE WORST LINE. It was meant v lovingly."

‌



View 5 Images Ariana dated Ricky Alvarez for over a year before they split in July 2016 (Image: John Shearer/Getty Images for Kitty Purry, Inc)

Ariana's decision to take a break follows the music video release for her single Petal, taken from her eighth studio album, which sparked renewed online speculation rearding her health and weight loss.

The star has previously spoken about the heavy emotional toll of public scrutiny. In a candid 2024 interview addressing the pressure to "to always look perfect", she noted that she had been "a specimen in a petri dish since I was 16 or 17. I have heard it all. I have heard every form of what is wrong with me. And then you fix it and then it is wrong for different reasons."

Article continues below

"It is hard to protect yourself from that noise. I think that it's something that is uncomfortable no matter what scale you're experiencing it on." From what you are wearing, to your body, to your face, to your everything – there is a comfortability that people have commenting on that that I think is really dangerous. I think it is dangerous for all parties involved."

In November, she reshared the interview on her social media, adding a simple caption: "As a loving reminder to all".

News.title: 'Make living rooms cosy' with £20 B&M piece that can be used as 'extra seating'
News.content:
'Make living rooms cosy' with £20 B&M piece that can be used as 'extra seating'

Shoppers can give their living spaces an extra dimension with an item now on sale at B&M

View 3 Images B&M has launched a host of new deals across its 700-strong stores (Image: B&M)

Transform living rooms with an item that can double-up as "extra seating" now on store shelves at B&M. The high street brand, which has over 500 stores nationwide, claims it can "give spaces a cosy update".

‌



B&M sells a wide range of affordable furniture and homeware, including side tables, desks, chairs, curtains and a growing collection of home decor, garden essentials and beauty products. It's also stocking lounge pieces that are said to add an extra level of comfort to a home's most lived-in areas.

‌



The Home Collection Cube Pouffe is retailing for £20 and is only available for in-store collection. Interested buyers are urged to check stock levels at their local B&M branch using the online store finder before heading out on their latest shopping trip.

‌



View 3 Images The Home Collection Cube Pouffe at B&M (Image: B&M)

A pouffe is a compact, padded piece of furniture that can be used as a footrest, occasional seat or decorative accent in a living room or bedroom. Many designs are lightweight enough to move around the home, making them a practical way to add extra seating or comfort without taking up as much space as an armchair or stool.

‌



Describing the piece, B&M said: "Give your living room a cosy update with the Home Collection Cube Pouffe. Featuring an eye-catching, modern design and compact size which makes it easy to fit into any space.

"Use as a footstool to put your feet up after a long day, or as extra seating when guests pop round."It has a sleek green design that could complement a range of interior styles and colour schemes.

View 3 Images The Home Collection Square Inflatable Footstool at B&M (Image: B&M)

Article continues below

Measuring a compact 38 x 38 x 38cm, it offers flexibility when it comes to placement and should fit easily into most living rooms. Its lightweight build also means it can be moved to another location if needed.

Customers hoping to find out more should visit the B&M website. There, they can discover additional product information and images, as well as browse a selection of similar items also on sale such as the Home Collection Square Inflatable Footstool for £12.

"Add a blend of style and functionality to your home with the Square Inflatable Footstool," reads the product description. "This contemporary footstool, in a neutral colourway, will add style to any room in the home."

News.title: Glasgow hailed as 'blueprint for future of Commonwealth Games' after major success
News.content:
Glasgow hailed as 'blueprint for future of Commonwealth Games' after major success

A new format using exisiting facilities proved to be a "Games changer". The event sold more than 430,000 tickets to show that it was a real Box Office success.

The King and The Queen's entrance to the Opening Ceremony of Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games

Glasgow 2026 was today hailed as a 'blueprint' for future Commonwealth Games.

‌



The event ended with a message to the rest of the world - the new format using exisiting facilities is a "Games changer". It sold more than 430,000 tickets to show that it was a real Box Office success.

‌



And Phil Batty, chief executive of Glasgow 2026, said: "We have created a Games that will inspire more nations to host. Probably more importantly, it is one that every nation feels it could host at some point in the next 100 years.

‌



"The future of the Commonwealth Games was in jeopardy. Glasgow saved the Commonwealth Games but it also reinvented the Commonwealth Games."

Jim Kerr and Simple Minds brought down the curtain on the event at the closing ceremony. The Games' projected cost was £162.6m compared with £543m for Glasgow 2014 and £680m for Birmingham 2022.

View 3 Images Jim Kerr of Simple Minds at the closing ceremony of Glasgow 2026 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Prince Edward shares sweet moment with Prince Louis at Commonwealth Games READ MORE :

The public backed the Games as netball proved to be the most popular sport selling more than 100,000 tickets. English powerlifter Mark Swan won the first gold medal of the 215 that were on offer.

The rising star from Seaham, Co Durham, said it had provided an 'unforgettable experience'. The more compact 23rd edition featured 215 medal events compared to 261 when the city last staged the Games in 2014. It also saw a record 47 para-sports events, which included the symbolic first gold medal.

View 3 Images Jim Kerr of Simple Minds on stage at the closing ceremony of Glasgow 2026 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Australia dominated the medal table by amassing 171 followed by England with 110. The host nation finished fifth, with 39 medals, behind Canada and India.

It was a performance described by First Minister John Swinney as "truly historic". Welsh star Emma Finucane created history by becoming the first sprint cyclist to win four track gold medals at the same Games.

Louise Hoskins became the oldest Commonwealth Games gold medallist, winning the para-bowls women's pairs title for Australia at the age of 76 years and 173 days. And legendary South African swimmer Chad le Clos became the most decorated athlete in the 96-year history of the event with 21 medals.

Article continues below

View 3 Images Fireworks closed Glasgow 2026 (Image: Jane Barlow/PA Wire)

Prince William and Princess Kate were among those who took in the action with their children. Mile world record holder Josh Kerr produced another thrilling triumph in the mile, which last featured at the Games in 1966.

The star repaid fans by taking 45 minutes to pose for selfies and autographs after his emotional medal ceremony.

News.title: Shoppers warned of higher prices and shortages due to drought conditions
News.content:
Shoppers warned of higher prices and shortages due to drought conditions

Farming leaders call on government to step in as extreme weather forces many to complete harvest weeks early - with reports of unprecedented numbers throwing in the towel and selling up

View 3 Images Weeks without rain has caused havoc for farmers across England and Wales (Image: Geoffrey Swaine/Shutterstock)

The government has been urged to take action amid warnings that shoppers face higher food prices and possible shortages because of the prolonged drought.

‌



Tom Bradshaw, president of the National Farmers’ Union, called on ministers to help support the building of reservoirs on farms as part of wider measures. “Water security is food security and food security is part of our national security,” Mr Bradshaw said.

‌



It came as heat health alerts were issued for most of England as temperatures are forecast to reach the mid-30s centigrade. That followed what has been the driest July on record for England and Wales.

‌



View 3 Images Some farmers have been forced to complete their harvest many weeks early this year (Image: David Hartley/Shutterstock)

Parched conditions have caused havoc for farmers. Many arable farmers have been forced to bring forward their wheat harvest by several weeks - in some cases the earliest for at least 20 years - because of the extreme weather, with an impact on yields - the amount produced.

Mr Bradshaw also explained that livestock farmers are using their winter feed rations because they cannot grow grass. He said: “It does feel like there is going to be some shortages of (food) products.”

‌



Potato production is another crop heavily impacted as about half of what is produced needs irrigation. “The reservoirs are almost empty,” Mr Bradshaw added.

He went on: “We need to think about the resilience of our food system as a national priority. We need to adapt, we want to adapt, but we also need the government to recognise that this needs to happen urgently and we need their support.

View 3 Images Lower wheat harvest could feed through to bread prices (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Mr Bradshaw argued tor farmers to be given tax breaks to build water storage systems on their land.

“Those other countries around the world that we currently rely on to produce our food and vegetables, their climates are changing as well,” he said.

Anthony Hopkins, director of cereals and oilseeds at the Agriculture and Horticulture Development Board, said: “Across much of the UK, combine (harvesters) have been rolling earlier than usual this year, with many farmers working through the night to avoid the most extreme daytime temperatures."

‌



Some farmers, already reeling from soaring fertiliser and other costs, have decided to throw in the towel, with reports from agents of unprecedented numbers of farms being put up for sale.

There are warnings that food prices in shops could rise, adding to the cost of living squeeze on millions of families. New PM Andy Burnham has made tackling living costs a key priority for his new government.

Dr Anna Murgatroyd, a lecturer in hydrology at Newcastle University, said: “One thing I imagine we will start to see is food prices increasing, and we are probably likely to see fewer food products from Britain on our shelves - we might even start to see shortages depending on what happens over the next couple of weeks and months.”

Article continues below

Farmer Andrew Ward, in Lincolnshire, said the last rain it had was on June 11, with 4mm. “You cannot grow crops and produce food without water, it’s as simple as that,” he said, adding that it had finished its wheat harvest a month early and with a lower yield because of the weather. “Across the country we are going to be short of wheat, there is no doubt about it,” he warned.

News.title: Boy thrown from Tate Modern balcony finally leaves hospital as family issue update
News.content:
Boy thrown from Tate Modern balcony finally leaves hospital as family issue update

The family of a French boy who was thrown from a viewing platform at the Tate Modern art gallery in 2019 say he has a 'smile back on his face' after being discharged from hospital

View 2 Images Emergency crews at the scene of the incident at Tate Modern on August 4, 2019 (Image: PA)

The family of a boy who was thrown from a viewing platform at the Tate Modern art gallery say he has a "smile back on his face" after finally being discharged from hospital.

‌



The French youngster was six years old when he was seriously injured in the attack by then-teenager Jonty Bravery at the London art gallery on August 4, 2019.

‌



The boy, who was on holiday with his parents, survived a 100ft fall but suffered life-changing injuries, including a bleed on the brain and multiple broken bones.

‌



Almost seven years after the incident, his family, who call him "notre petit chevalier" - our little knight - said in an update on a GoFundMe page that he was able to return to school briefly before the summer holidays.

View 2 Images Jonty Bravery (Image: PA)

Drivers have stolen nearly £200,000 of fuel from UK forecourts every day since Iran war began READ MORE :

They said: "We wanted to let you know that our little knight has finally left the hospital! His hospital stay was kept as short as possible because, despite our daily presence and encouragement, our son was becoming deeply disheartened and kept asking when he could go back to class and see his friends.

‌



"It was a great joy for him to return to school shortly before the summer holidays; since the lessons were well tailored to his needs and challenges, he was able to start learning again, and reuniting with his teachers and classmates put a smile back on his face."

In April, his family said his recovery had taken a "sad step backwards", but their latest update was far more positive.

The GoFundMe page was set up by nurse Vicky Diplacto, from Surrey, whose brother was paralysed in an incident overseas. The crowdfunding campaign, which aims to cover the French boy's medical costs, has so far raised more than £500,000.

‌



The boy continues to undergo intensive rehabilitation, including physiotherapy, speech therapy and neuropsychology.

To celebrate the end of his hospital treatment, his family are treating him to a tandem paragliding flight and a seaside getaway with friends.

He also plans to resume his adaptive swimming lessons, along with maths tutoring to help him catch up on the schooling he has missed.

‌



His family said: "It will certainly be a busy summer. We are going to try to fully recharge his batteries (and our own) before the start of the school year, and to get back to a family routine as normal as possible."

Bravery, now 24, was living in supported accommodation at the time of the attack but had been allowed out unsupervised. A court later heard he intended to select and kill someone.

Bravery, who was 17 at the time, pleaded guilty to attempted murder and was handed a life sentence with a minimum term of 15 years.

Article continues below

He was back in court earlier this year and was jailed for 16 weeks after being found guilty of assaulting two nurses at Broadmoor, a high-security psychiatric hospital in Berkshire, in September 2024.

In 2020, he was given a 14-week jail sentence after admitting to attacking staff at the same hospital.

News.title: English FA set to withdraw support for Fifa president Infantino
News.content:
The English Football Association is set to write to Fifa president Gianni Infantino withdrawing its support for him amid the fallout from his scrapped plans to sell off stakes in Fifa competitions to private investors.

It comes as Uefa threatens legal action over the proposals and Wales publicly withdraw backing for Infantino's bid to continue as Fifa president.

Next March, Infantino is set to stand for re-election for a fourth and final term as president and would need 106 votes from Fifa's 211 members to win.

Sources have told BBC Sport the Scottish FA's position on the future of Infantino remains aligned with Uefa's lack of confidence in the 56-year-old.

Infantino's leadership had already been publicly questioned by football's governing bodies in Europe, North and Central America and the Caribbean, with Uefa and Concacaf releasing statements criticising the plans.

Fifa and Infantino wanted to create a commercial subsidiary to run its main events, including its World Cups, and external investors would have been able to buy stakes in it.

World football's governing body said it would "invite third parties to make minority, non-controlling investments" in a new subsidiary called Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE).

As first reported by The Telegraph, Uefa said in a letter to Infantino "it is actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints (together, the 'proceedings') arising out of and in connection with the FFE plan proposed by Fifa".

Uefa added it wants "immediate steps" to "preserve all documents and electronically stored information" in Fifa's possession "independent" of their internal policies that may result in "routine document destruction or deletion".

BBC Sport has approached Fifa for comment.

News.title: Mother has ground-breaking surgery while pregnant to treat baby
News.content:
Doctors have used ground-breaking surgery on an unborn baby to successfully correct a birth defect while he was still inside the womb.

His mother, Maisie Savage, from London, was operated on by doctors in the US while she was 26 weeks pregnant.

Baby Theo, who is now five months old and thriving, had gastroschisis, where the belly button does not develop properly, causing the intestines to grow externally.

Doctors partially exposed his mother's womb and then gently pushed his organs back inside his abdomen using keyhole surgery.

He was the third baby in the world to benefit from the first-of-its-kind clinical trial.

Maisie, 29, and Theo's father, Josh French, 36, both teachers, say they are incredibly relieved by the success of the pioneering surgery.

"He's a little miracle, isn't he?" Maisie told BBC News.

But they both know things could have been very different.

The serious birth defect affects one in 3,000 UK babies each year. In the best-case scenarios, babies can require weeks in intensive care and nutritional feeding through a tube or IV and corrective surgery.

For the most complex cases, like Theo's, outcomes are far more serious with up to six months in neonatal intensive care, multiple surgeries, IV nutritional feeding for up to two years, and a possible intestinal transplant.

Even with the highest level of medical care, one in 10 babies will die.

News.title: Reform says it would use Navy to stop small boats
News.content:
Reform UK says it would use the military to forcibly return small boat migrants to France.

The plans, unveiled on Monday, suggest military personnel would accompany migrants back to ports on the other side of the English Channel, overriding French objections if necessary.

The party claim the proposals would form the "largest military operation" in the Channel since World War Two.

But opponents have branded the plan unworkable, with the Conservatives saying the policy is not credible.

Under Reform UK's plans if it enters government, military-crewed inflatable boats deployed from Navy patrol vessels would be used to "come alongside" boats crossing the Channel.

Border Force officers and police would be tasked with arresting people in the boats, before they would then be returned to France or Belgium by Royal Navy personnel or Marines.

Speaking at a news conference to announce the plans, Reform's home affairs spokesman Zia Yusuf said the party would seek to disembark them at ports with the agreement of the French government.

But he claimed the party would show "unflinching resolve" to make sure returns happened in any circumstances.

"We would far rather disembark people in port, walk people down a gangway and hand them to the French authorities properly," he added.

"But if the Elysee Palace refuses, make no mistake - His Majesty's Royal Marines will disembark them safely on the very shore they left that morning".

Reform leader Nigel Farage added: "When you think about it, what is the Royal Navy for?

"If the Royal Navy is not there to protect this country from invasion, then, frankly, I can't see what its purpose is."

More than 2,000 migrants have arrived in the UK on small boats since Burnham became prime minister, and 326 people crossed the English Channel on Saturday. Home Office figures show crossings so far this year are down around 43% compared to the same period in 2025.

The number of small boats crossing the Channel have been on a downward trend since it peaked in 2022, Home Office figures show.

Yusuf described the scheme as "humanitarian" and insisted it would be compatible with rules under the European Convention on Human Rights as Article 2 protects the right to life.

International conventions on the sea allow for states to pick people up from boats if they are in danger of being lost but do not allow for them to be taken to another country without that nation's consent.

Yusuf accepted that the UK and France may have "a diplomatic argument" if French authorities were to refuse to accept migrants escorted back to its shores, but insisted they have a "commitment under international law" to process migrants.

But Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh told BBC Radio 4 Today programme this would mean spending "a lot of time arguing with France".

She said the government "absolutely needs to get a grip" on small boat crossings, but said Prime Minister Andy Burnham's team was cracking down on criminal gangs and boosting enforcement.

The prime minister visited Dover at the weekend, where he said the government was "changing the whole approach" to small boats, as the numbers of enforcement officers tackling people-smuggling gangs doubled on both sides of the Channel.

According to the Home Office, the number of National Crime Agency (NCA) officers tackling smuggling gangs facilitating small boat crossings had risen to almost 800 from 376 at the start of 2025.

Reacting to Reform's proposals, retired Royal Navy commander Tom Sharpe told the BBC the UK's border force is better suited to managing migrant arrivals than the navy.

Warships designed for tasks including anti-submarine defences "are not best used for ferrying people around", he explained.

"You're better off using an actual ferry," he said.

Meanwhile, Conservative shadow home secretary Chris Philp insisted that leaving the European Convention on Human Rights should be the government's priority to tackle illegal migration.

"That would enable us to deport every single illegal immigrant within a week of arrival," he told BBC Breakfast. "Either back to their country of origin if possible, or a safe third country, for example Rwanda, if not."

He said this would bring a "deterrent effect" as migrants would no longer cross the channel if they knew they would be deported straight away.

"Reform's policy I am afraid as usual is on the back of a fag packet. By the way I am not averse to taking actions at sea if it's credible but Reform policy isn't credible."

News.title: Newspaper columnist and broadcaster Rod Liddle dies aged 66
News.content:
Newspaper columnist and broadcaster Rod Liddle has died aged 66 after a short illness.

Liddle's children paid tribute to their father, who they described as their guide "on how to live an extraordinary life", while CEO of News UK, Rebekah Brooks, described him as "an inimitable journalistic force."

Brooks added that "he challenged conventional thinking and left an indelible mark on British journalism."

Liddle, a columnist for the Sun and the Sunday Times, died at The James Cook University Hospital in Middlesbrough on Sunday evening.
