News.title: X Factor finalist denies murdering influencer by running her over with car
News.content:
A former X Factor finalist has denied murdering a social media influencer by running her over with a car in central London.

Gabrielle Carrington of Manchester, allegedly struck Klaudia Zakrzewska outside Inca nightclub in Argyll Street, Soho, at 04:30 BST on 19 April.

The 29-year-old appeared at the Old Bailey by video link from Bronzefield prison to deny the charge. She had been initially charged with attempted murder but that was changed to murder after Zakrzewska died from her injuries six days later.

Carrington, who was not represented in court by a barrister, also denied a second charge of causing grievous bodily harm with intent to security guard Anoush Chyche.

The defendant was not asked to enter a plea to a third charge of driving with excess alcohol.

Family members of the victims shook their heads as the accused read out her pleas.

Judge Sarah Whitehouse KC confirmed the trial would be held at the same court from 5 January.

Carrington appeared emotional on the video link, wiping tears from her face throughout the hearing and was placed into custody afterwards.

News.title: Presenter Tony Livesey leaves BBC Radio 5 Live after 16 years
News.content:
Presenter Tony Livesey has left BBC Radio 5 Live after 16 years at the station, the corporation has announced.

Livesey stepped back from his weekday late night talk show in June, following allegations made against his former newspaper boss David Sullivan.

He had previously worked as editor-in-chief of Sullivan's Daily and Sunday Sport publications.

Several women have accused Sullivan, a billionaire businessman and West Ham co-owner, of abusing his power and preying on them for sex, in some cases when they were teenagers. Sullivan has strongly denied the allegations.

The claims against Sullivan were made in a joint investigation by the Times and BBC Panorama.

The BBC previously said Livesey had asked to take a break from presenting his programme while the issues raised by the investigation were being examined.

One alleged victim said that Livesey had arranged a meeting between her and Sullivan in 1999.

Livesey said he had "no recollection" of introducing the young woman to Sullivan and that it was "not part" of his job to do so.

He added that he had "great sympathy for a woman who may have become a victim", but rejected any suggestion that he had played "any role whatsoever in that scenario" and said he found the allegation "abhorrent".

In an email sent to 5 Live staff on Monday morning, the station's controller Heidi Dawson said he had now decided to leave.

"Tony has asked me to pass on his heartfelt thanks to the brilliant colleagues at 5 Live who he has had the pleasure of working with over the years," she wrote.

"I know many of you have also really enjoyed working with Tony, and we wish him well for all his future endeavours."

The award-winning presenter worked for the BBC from 2006, the same year he left the newspapers, appearing on 5 Live from 2010 onwards including a successful stint helming its drivetime show.

He won radio awards - ARIA and APAs - for his reporting on how it feels to lose your mother as a child, and an ARIAS gold award after he was asked by the late Dame Deborah James to conduct her final interview.

His topical three-hour programme was broadcast on 5 Live from Monday to Thursday, featuring interviews and phone calls from listeners.

News.title: Reform UK's Richard Tice investigated by parliamentary standards watchdog
News.content:
Reform UK's deputy leader Richard Tice is being investigated by the parliamentary standards watchdog over an allegation he failed to declare an interest.

The investigation was opened on Tuesday 28 July and was published on the Parliamentary Standards Commissioner website on Monday.

Tice, the MP for Boston and Skegness, said the complaint related to a Commons debate about Israeli influence and whether he should have referenced his register of interests.

Reform said Tice did not mention in his 22 June speech that he had been on a trip to Israel last September, funded by a pro-Israel lobbying group.

The trip has been listed in Tice's Declaration of Members' Interests., external

The investigation relates to Rule 6 in the parliamentary code of conduct, which states: "Members must always be open and frank in declaring any relevant interest in any proceeding of the House or its committees, and in any communications with ministers, members, public officials or public office holders."

The Parliament's guidance to the code of conduct states that MPs can refer to their entry in the register of interests but adds: "Such a reference will not suffice on its own, as the declaration must provide sufficient information to convey the nature of the interest without the listener or the reader having to have recourse to the Register or other publication."

A few days before the parliamentary standards commissioner opened this inquiry, the BBC learned a police investigation had been opened into payments to Reform UK by a company controlled by Tice in the run-up to the general election.

Tice, who was party chairman at the time, was the sole owner and controller of Britain Means Business, which made two donations of Â£250,000 to Reform UK.

At the time, Tice told the BBC: "This is the first I have heard of it - if true why are the Met Police briefing the BBC before contacting interested parties? Is the Met leadership now engaged in the widespread politically motivated smear campaign against Reform and its leaders?"

Tice has said the money was given to his firm by Fiona Cottrell, a significant donor to Reform UK and mother of a convicted fraudster with close links to party leader Nigel Farage.

Farage has also had an investigation launched into a potential failure to declare an interest, which relates to a Â£5m gift from crypto-billionaire Christopher Harborne before he became an MP.

That investigation was opened on 13 May but suspended on 8 July when Farage quit to stand in the Clacton by-election - the full list of 34 candidates can be seen here.

If Farage is re-elected, that investigation will restart.

Separately, an investigation has also been opened into DUP MP Sammy Wilson, for an allegation of failure to declare an interest. The DUP has been contacted for comment.

News.title: Xbox Series X price hiked by £170 due to rising memory chip costs
News.content:
Microsoft has increased the price of Xbox consoles worldwide, citing rising memory and storage chip costs.

Its premium Series X console with a disc drive will now cost Â£670, when it previously retailed for Â£500.

Meanwhile a baseline Xbox Series S console now costs Â£430 - a roughly 43% increase on its previous Â£300 price tag.

It is among a host of tech firms to have told consumers that spiralling component costs mean they must charge more, with rival Sony hiking PlayStation 5 prices by Â£90 in March.

Microsoft said in June it had "hoped another price increase would not be necessary", but blamed the rising cost of console storage and memory for needing to raise prices on consumers.

In the US, its basic consoles rose by $100 to $499, and the cost of a console with more memory increased by $150 to $749.

Similar increases have been revealed in the EU as well - where a Series S console with more storage will cost roughly â¬200 more than it did before.

As well as Sony increasing PlayStation prices, Steam Machine maker Valve launched its PC-console hybrid at a much higher cost than expected.

Both likewise pointed to mounting costs for the hardware and storage components needed to power their devices.

News.title: How parents and pupils took on 'cruel', 'authoritarian' schools - and won
News.content:
To avoid getting into trouble, 14-year-old Amelia says she decided to stop drinking water at school so she would not need the toilet.

Her school, Camborne Science and International Academy in Cornwall, had introduced strict disciplinary policies, which included limiting toilet visits during classes, according to pupils and former teachers.

New discipline rules were implemented when the school was taken over in January 2024 by the Athena Learning Trust, which runs six secondary schools in Devon and Cornwall.

Amelia's mother, Kayley, believes these strict policies resulted in her daughter becoming ill from a series of serious infections caused by not drinking.

Hundreds of parents, including Kayley, have campaigned against the way Athena run its schools.

Across Devon and Cornwall, there have been public meetings, school-gate protests and online petitions. Local MPs and councillors have also backed concerned parents.

The opposition to Athena now appears to have paid off - with the trust announcing last month that it was planning to disband and transfer all its schools to other trusts.

It said that trustees had "listened carefully to feedback" and recognised the "clear need for change".

BBC Panorama has spoken to nearly 100 pupils, parents and former teachers from Athena schools, who say levels of discipline went too far. Many pupils and parents queued to talk to us at two town hall meetings we arranged.

The way the schools had been run was "authoritarian" and "cruel", some said.

"You're constantly scared you're going to do something wrong," one student with ADHD told us, while a former music teacher said the strict discipline had meant his lessons were taught in silence.

News.title: Almost £200,000 of fuel stolen from UK forecourts every day since Iran war began
News.content:
UK drivers have stolen almost Â£200,000 of fuel from petrol stations on average every day since the Iran war broke out and sent prices soaring, according to industry analysis.

Incidents of fuel being taken from forecourts without payment have risen by a fifth in the five months since 28 February, figures from Forecourt Eye suggest.

The conflict in the Middle East severely disrupted oil supplies across the region, triggering a rise in wholesale prices and subsequent increase in costs at the pump in the UK.

Forecourt Eye said the value of the stolen fuel is estimated to have risen by 48% compared with the five months before the war - to reach an estimated daily average of Â£194,000.

The fuel theft prevention company added petrol stations are reporting an increase in "abuse, intimidation and violence from frustrated customers".

The figures are based on a representative sample of 550 forecourts, comparing the five months prior to the outbreak with the five months after it started, and extrapolated to the UK's 8,359 forecourts.

The number of incidents recorded at the forecourts in the sample equates to 2,872 daily incidents on average at forecourts across the UK in the months after war began, up from around 2,400.

They include people driving off without an attempt to pay, and people claiming they have no way to pay after filling their vehicle.

The volume of stolen fuel rose by 24% - up from an estimated 87,000 litres to 108,900 litres a day across all forecourts.

In response, Forecourt Eye said it would partner with facial recognition company Facewatch to offer more than 2,000 retailers free access to crime reporting technology from the autumn.

News.title: Heat health alerts in England as temperatures set to reach 34C
News.content:
Amber and yellow heat health alerts are now in effect across much of England, with temperatures expected to reach 34C in some areas.

The amber alerts, external, issued by the UK Health Security Agency, cover London, the south east, the east of England and the East Midlands, until 0900 BST on Wednesday 5 August.

They warn that significant impacts are likely across health and social care services due to the high temperatures, including a rise in deaths, particularly among vulnerable people.

Less severe yellow heat heat alerts have also been issued for the same period for the north west, Yorkshire and the Humber, West Midlands and the south west.

News.title: Son who kept mum's body in freezer for years collected £78k of her benefits
News.content:
A man who kept his dead mother in a chest freezer in the living room of the family home for nearly three years and continued to collect her pension and benefits has been sentenced to two years and four months in prison.

Christopher Phillips, 60, was arrested after the body of Sylvia Phillips, 89, was found by officers in February at Poplar Crescent, Porthcawl, Bridgend county.

She had died in March 2023.

Phillips had told doctors he "did not want to let her go" and "wanted more time" after her death.

Sylvia Phillips was discovered wrapped in a leopard print silk blanket, with yellow and pink roses placed on her body, as well as a birthday card signed from him and the family dog Tina.

"To Mum, from Christopher and Tina," the card read.

Phillips admitted three offences including failing to lawfully and decently bury his mother and continuing to claim her pension and benefits including housing benefits and winter fuel allowances.

Merthyr Tydfil Crown Court heard Phillips had been adopted by Sylvia Phillips at the age of two and was "exceptionally close" to her.

The day after she died on 8 March 2023 her son held her in his arms and told her he would look after her, the court was told.

Two days after her death, Phillips bought a chest freezer from AO.com, placing it in the dining room of the semi-detached home. She remained there until her body was discovered by police who carried out a welfare check requested by her GP.

The court was told that the local medical practice had made repeated attempts to contact her but were denied access by her son.

When police went to the house, Phillips said his mother had moved to London and did not want to undergo medical tests.

The court heard officers became suspicious, with Phillips seen trembling and fidgeting. He ran upstairs and later could be heard telling a girlfriend on the phone that the "police are going to arrest me, you've got the will".

News.title: Glasgow hailed for saving Games as baton passes to Amdavad
News.content:
The man responsible for delivering Glasgow 2026 said the city had "saved and reinvented" the Commonwealth Games, three years after its future was plunged into doubt.

Ahead of Sunday's closing ceremony - which featured a dazzling fireworks display over the River Clyde - Phil Batty recalled how Glasgow stepped up when the original hosts pulled out.

And he believes the legacy of the sustainable, scaled-back Games will shape the future of the multi-sports event.

The Commonwealth flag has been handed over to the Indian city of Amdavad, also known as Ahmedabad, which will stage the centenary event in 2030.

But Batty said Glasgow's decision to host the event for a second time in 12 years would never be forgotten.

He told BBC Scotland News: "We have created a Games here that will inspire more nations to host but, probably more importantly, that every nation feels it could host at some point in the next 100 years."

News.title: Jade Goody's widower Jack Tweed admits drug driving
News.content:
Jack Tweed, the widower of Big Brother star Jade Goody, has been banned from driving after admitting being behind the wheel under the influence of cannabis.

He was stopped on Three Mile Hill, near Chelmsford in Essex, on 6 December 2025 and arrested after he failed a roadside drug swipe.

At Chelmsford Magistrates' Court on Monday, Tweed, 39, pleaded guilty to one charge of driving a motor vehicle with a proportion of a specified controlled drug above the specified limit.

He apologised to the court and said he had taken the drug to "help me sleep" after experiencing depression and anxiety.

More from Essex:

The court heard that Tweed, who appeared on Celebrity Big Brother UK in 2007, was taken to a police station for a blood sample which recorded 5.6 micrograms of delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol â the main active component of cannabis â in his system, exceeding the limit of two micrograms.

The court fined Tweed Â£692 and ordered him to pay a surcharge of Â£277 and costs of Â£85.

News.title: I didn't know I'd been hosting a parasite for years - until the most intense pain of my life
News.content:
Jones remembers the May 2016 night when he went into hospital â he was supposed to go out to a dinner with his wife Eileen, but he stayed at home as he felt unwell.

"I hadn't been able to control the pain, and it was more intense than anything I had before.

"Then about midnight, we had to call the ambulance, and they took me to Nevill Hall. Whatever they gave me there cured the pain. I haven't experienced pain like that before."

Jones was in hospital for 10 days, and says the doctors there suspected he had hydatid cysts immediately.

He said: "There was a lot of it around this area at the time, and I remember the Ministry of Agriculture giving worming treatment to the dogs on the local farms.

"Whether they could see that I was an old sheep farmer or not, that might have had a bearing on it. We had plenty of experience in this area â Breconshire as a whole â of hydatid cysts, people that have suffered through it, numerous examples."

Jones was then referred to "the main expert on hydatid cysts" in London where he had two operations in 2018 and 2019 to remove them, one from each lung.

"I swapped two cysts for two scars on the ribs," he said, adding that he still has a cyst on his liver, which surgeons decided not to remove.

News.title: Conservatives call for greater use of facial recognition from police
News.content:
The Conservatives have called for the greater use of facial recognition technology to investigate crimes.

Shadow home secretary Chris Philp wants to make it a requirement for officers to run images of suspects through facial recognition software, where they have been captured on CCTV, mobile phones or camera doorbells.

He also wants officers to follow up when geo-tagged items - including phones, laptops, tablets, bikes and cars - are pinging their location at a suspect's address, as well as tackling stolen goods being sold in plain sight.

A Home Office spokesperson said the government was investing heavily in facial recognition technology.

"This government is already turning the tide on crime," they added.

Philp said the Conservative's Take Back Our Streets plan would put all three elements into practice, backed up by 10,000 extra police officers, which he claimed would be fully funded by Â£800 million per year.

"The public expects clear evidence to always be followed up," he said.

"When they show the police an image of a suspect or the location of stolen goods they want action, not just a crime number."

Labour has pledged an extra 13,000 neighbourhood police by the end of this Parliament. An additional 3,814 officers have been hired between April 2025 and March this year.

Philp praised the existing facial recognition database, which contains images of about 10 million people that can be face-matched using AI, but said what was missing was a requirement on a force to always use it.

Similarly, he said, where a stolen device is pinging its location at an address, an officer will be required to knock on the door.

He added that officers would be required to follow listings of stolen goods advertised online and recover belongings where possible.

"These are the basics the public expect," he said.

Hundreds of migrants have established a makeshift camp on a beach in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, as local authorities grapple with the aftermath of a massive border surge last week.

Spain estimates that 69,500 migrants have been returned to Morocco over the past four days, a figure that surpasses initial projections of around 50,000 arrivals in Ceuta last Thursday.

Ceuta, on the North African coast, is an autonomous city of Spain.

The official death toll stands at 72 on the Spanish side of the border, with 11 fatalities reported on the Moroccan side.

Many of those remaining cited shop closures leading to food shortages, hostility from local residents, and the inability to continue their journey to the Spanish mainland as reasons for their predicament.

Ceuta, along with Spain's other North African enclave, Melilla, frequently experiences attempted crossings by migrants seeking to reach Europe.

open image in gallery Migrants sleep on a beach in Ceuta ( Reuters )

Footage from the beach showed scores of migrants resting on the sand of El Trampolin beach, many wrapped in towels against the wind, while army and police vehicles patrolled nearby.

Juan Jesus Vivas, Ceuta's leader, told broadcaster Telecinco that between 3,000 and 5,000 migrants remain in the enclave, adding that its two reception centres – one for adults and another for minors – had "collapsed".

Local official Alberto Gaitan said that the city is currently processing 862 migrant minors, who are afforded special legal protections against deportation.

Crisis sparks diplomatic tensions within EU

The crisis has fuelled anti-immigration rhetoric throughout Europe and sparked diplomatic tensions within the European Union over border policy, and Spain has accused some partners of an unhelpful and polarising response.

Foreign Minister Jose Manuel Albares said on Monday that Spain had previously supported other EU countries during migration crises and now expects the same backing.

open image in gallery A migrant prays while waiting on the beach ( Reuters )

The bloc has called an emergency video conference meeting of interior ministers to take place on Tuesday to discuss the crisis.

Mr Albares accused Italy’s government of helping to amplify misinformation.

He said that Morocco had immediately offered police support and had not attached conditions to its cooperation, allowing for the rapid return of most of those who crossed.

But Mr Vivas, Ceuta’s leader, was critical of the Moroccan government, saying that there was a widespread perception within Ceuta that it had allowed, if not orchestrated, the crisis.

"Morocco has shown us that it isn't reliable. There's no alternative but to put in place whatever means are necessary to ensure it cannot do this again," Mr Vivas told the Spanish language newspaper El Pais.

On Sunday, Morocco's Interior Ministry blamed the surge on misinformation on social media, human trafficking networks, and misinterpretation of a Spanish court ruling banning immediate returns of migrants intercepted at sea. That was in line with Spain’s official view.

open image in gallery Thousands of migrants remain in Ceuta after the mass border crossing ( Reuters )

Spain says Morocco allowed mass crossing

According to reports by El Pais and the Spanish radio station Cadena SER, citing officials familiar with the matter, Spanish intelligence services have concluded that Morocco did not plan the mass crossing, but allowed it to happen.

Moroccan border controls were gradually relaxed during July and were allegedly removed as crowds surged toward the Tarajal crossing during Morocco's Throne Day holiday, the reports said.

Morocco's Interior Ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

In its Sunday statement, it said that Morocco is "committed to strengthening international cooperation and coordination in combating irregular migration and human trafficking".

Spain's Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said on Saturday that the foreign intelligence agency CNI, which is controlled by the Defence Ministry, did not warn him of an imminent surge. El Pais said that had caused tensions between the two ministries.

An Interior Ministry spokesperson downplayed the reported tensions.

Defence Minister Margarita Robles declined to say whether the CNI had any prior intelligence of the mass crossing, adding its work was secret and praising the "exceptional" work of Spanish security services personnel.

More than one in five pregnant and breastfeeding women in eastern Chad have been found to be acutely malnourished, with severe funding shortages impacting access to food and healthcare.

More than 20 per cent of the women screened in the border town of Adré during the first six months of the year were suffering from moderate or severe acute malnutrition, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) said.

That is above the threshold used to define a critical humanitarian emergency, and the crisis is being worsened by a lack of support for host communities due to rules that restrict access to registered refugees.

Click here to watch Bel Trew’s new documentary –Hard Labour: Inside the global crisis killing mothers and babies

Since the war in neighbouring Sudan began, almost a million refugees have crossed into Chad, most of them women and children and more than 700,000 crossed through Adré.

Analysts have warned that the past two months have seen Chad increasingly drawn into Sudan’s civil war, with tensions rising in areas with scarce resources. Massive displacement, intercommunal tensions and cross-border violence are all pushing an already fragile region into deeper instability, according to the International Crisis Group.

Three-quarters of malnourished women belong to host communities, often excluded from aid programmes despite sharing already limited resources with arriving refugees.

“Having survived months of relentless violence, refugees arrive in Adré physically shattered, malnourished and deeply traumatised,” said Léa Ledru, MSF Project Coordinator in Adré. “[They are] met with a brutal new reality, finding themselves in areas where host communities are already living in poverty and humanitarian actors remain scarce.”

A Sudanese refugee woman from Al-Fashir carries a child in the a transit refugee camp in eastern Chad. ( Reuters )

Malnutrition among pregnant women drastically increases the risk of miscarriage, obstetric haemorrhage and premature birth.

Child malnutrition admissions at an MSF health centre in Adré also rose by 30 per cent.

It comes amid global aid funding shortfalls, with pipelines to treat acute malnutrition severely strained. Food aid is projected to run out in September.

Global aid fell by 23 per cent in 2025 compared to 2024, and is projected to drop by a further 5.8 per cent in 2026. Women and children have been disproportionately affected.

The US was the world’s largest donor, but President Donald Trump slashed foreign assistance programmes by 57 per cent last year, with the UK and Europe also reducing aid.

Hard-won successes in efforts to stop women and babies dying in childbirth have faced a serious setback as a result, reversing the trend in some countries .

It is particularly acute in parts of Africa as exposed in Hard Labour , a documentary by Bel Trew for Independent TV. The documentary lays out how efforts to stop women and babies dying in childbirth have been blunted in the Central African Republic and Nigeria, with aid cuts playing a significant role.

On Friday, the World Health Organisation called on countries to strengthen breastfeeding support and health systems ahead of World Breastfeeding Week next week.

Breastfeeding has significant health benefits for women and their babies, the WHO said, but support is disrupted in low-income countries and fragile humanitarian settings.

To mark the release of Hard Labour, The Independent is shining a light on the lifesaving work of the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) to raise awareness of the urgent maternal health needs of millions of women around the world. You can help save the life of a mother and baby by donating £8 for an emergency birth kit.

Sunday Times and Sun columnist Rod Liddle has died aged 66 after a short illness, his family has announced.

The veteran journalist worked in the media industry for decades, where he started his career at South Wales Echo. During his extensive career, he wrote for The Guardian, The Sunday Times, The Spectator and The Sun and hosted his own Times Radio show.

Liddle died at The James Cook University Hospital in Middlesbrough on Sunday evening.

In a statement issued by News UK, his children Wilder, Tyler and Emmy said: “We’re all very saddened and shocked at the sudden passing of our wonderful father. He raised us much as you might imagine, to be inquisitive, brave and always humorous.

“Even in hospital in the last few weeks, he consistently held the room and never let the awful situation show.

“He has left a legacy that we are all incredibly proud of, he will always be our guide on how to live an extraordinary life.”

open image in gallery Rod Liddle died at The James Cook University Hospital in Middlesbrough on Sunday evening ( Frantzesco Kangaris/The Independent )

Rebekah Brooks, CEO of News UK, said: “Everyone at News UK is deeply shocked and saddened to learn of the sudden death of Rod Liddle. Rod was an inimitable journalistic force – brilliant, provocative and immensely talented – whose sharp wit and uncompromising voice graced our pages and airwaves for decades.

“Whether writing for The Sunday Times and The Sun or broadcasting on Times Radio, he challenged conventional thinking and left an indelible mark on British journalism.

“Rod will be greatly missed by all his friends and colleagues at News, as well as by his many readers, listeners and viewers. Our thoughts and sincerest condolences are with his family and loved ones.”

Ben Taylor, editor of The Sunday Times, said: “Rod Liddle had a wonderful way with words and used his unique talent to speak for the readers, highlighting the cant and absurdity that bedevils modern life. He was also supremely entertaining and for years his column was the first that many turned to every Sunday. We will miss him desperately.”

open image in gallery Rod Liddle’s children paid tribute to their father who was their guide 'on how to live an extraordinary life' ( PA )

Victoria Newton, editor-in-chief of The Sun, said: “Rod was a brilliant, fearless columnist who was much loved by all at The Sun.

“A champion of press freedom, no topic was off-limits, and his writing – as funny as it was excoriating – was simply exceptional.

“A terrific observer of the frailties of our political class, he will be remembered for his razor sharp wit and for his huge intellect.

“But on The Sun floor he will also be remembered for his warmth and humour and for the belly laughs we had at his wildly entertaining lunches and dinners where he would hold court.

“He will be hugely missed by The Sun’s staff and by his many, many loyal readers.”

And Tim Levell, programme director of Times Radio, said: “Rod burst out of the speakers when he started his show on Times Radio. Listeners already knew about his wit and his proudly anti-conventional views.

“But his wide learning, dedication and comedic timing were a delight and surprise to many. His show brightened Saturday mornings enormously and he will be greatly missed.”

News.title: Man kept mother’s body in freezer for years while collecting £78k of her benefits
News.content:

A man has been sentenced to nearly two-and-a-half years in prison after storing his dead mother in a freezer and collecting more than £78,000 of her benefits.

Christopher Phillips, 60, previously pleaded guilty to preventing the lawful and decent burial of his mother Silvia Phillips, 89, at their home in Porthcawl, on the south coast of Wales.

He also pleaded guilty to two counts of fraud, by failing to notify the Department for Work and Pensions, as well as Bridgend County Borough Council, that his mother had died, over the same dates.

Phillips was sentenced at Merthyr Tydfil Crown Court on Monday.

Judge Tracey Lloyd-Clarke, the Recorder of Cardiff, sentenced him to two years and four months’ imprisonment.

Phillips had left work to become a full-time carer for his mother in the months leading up to her death on 8 March 2023, the court heard.

open image in gallery Phillips was sentenced at Merthyr Tydfil Crown Court ( PA )

The cause of her death remains unknown.

After she passed away, Phillips bought a chest freezer and used it to store her body inside the living room of the home.

The court heard that the body was covered with a leopard print throw and found alongside roses and a birthday card, reading “To Mum, from Christopher and Tina”, a reference to the family dog.

Phillips received a total of £78,190.92 in benefits following his mother’s death.

News.content:

Glasgow might have saved the Commonwealth Games, but don’t expect to see them back on these shores for a generation.

Four of the last seven editions have been staged in Great Britain, and it’s clear that Commonwealth Sport realises it needs to cut ties to the mother country for its future relevance.

Scotland gets its eternal thanks for stepping in at just 18 months’ notice when Australia said it couldn’t afford to host. Australian taxpayers ended up paying Glasgow £100m in compensation to stage the Games on their behalf and then duly topped the medal table with 70 golds.

“Glasgow has acted as a bridge to the future of the Commonwealth Games movement,” said Dr Donald Rukare, Commonwealth Sport president.

“Every host writes its own chapter, and Glasgow’s has been one of bravery, courage, friendship and, above all, outstanding innovation.”

India will host the centenary Games in 2030, and there are four private expressions of interest for 2034, with sports ministers having been wined and dined in Glasgow’s most expensive spots in recent days.

open image in gallery The baton has passed to India for the next Commonwealth Games ( Getty )

Nigeria has made no secret of its desire to become the first African host, while New Zealand believes a lower-cost approach to hosting finally gives it a chance to welcome the Commonwealth for the first time since 1990. Canada hasn’t hosted since 1994 either.

Insiders admit there is more chance of the Olympics coming back to the UK – with a bid mooted for the 2040s – before another Commonwealth Games.

For years, officials presented hosts with a long list of demands and requirements. Glasgow has changed all that. The power has shifted and that’s arguably no bad thing.

“It’s a much more collaborative process,” said Katie Sadlier, the Commonwealth Sport chief executive.

“We’re not telling hosts, ‘This is what you must do.’ Instead, we’re asking, ‘What are you trying to achieve?’ and then working with them to make that happen.

“We’ve set a guideline of around 15 to 17 sports, but if a future host comes to us with a proposal they believe works for them, we’ll sit down and work through it together. We’re not imposing rigid targets.

“We don’t want countries building facilities they don’t actually need just to host the Games. If a nation genuinely wants to build a stadium because it fits its long-term plans, that’s fine, but it shouldn’t automatically become part of the Games budget.

“We don’t want hosts spending huge amounts of money on things we don’t think are necessary any more. Glasgow is using existing venues, stakeholders have accepted reduced service levels, there are no fleets of VIP cars, and people are travelling by bus. Everyone has embraced that because they wanted the Commonwealth Games to happen.”

open image in gallery Josh Kerr provided one of the moments of the Games ( PA Wire )

But the Commonwealth movement can see the Games shifting away from the UK, a feeling reinforced by the BBC’s decision not to broadcast them free-to-air for the first time since 1954.

The next Games in India will feature 50 per cent more sports, but many at Commonwealth Sport still carry the scars of the Games in Delhi 16 years ago, which were so mired in corruption and incompetence there was a real chance, just days before they began, that they wouldn’t happen.

India, which currently leads the world in anti-doping violations, won 13 golds to finish fourth in the medal table here and is expected to stack the sports programme to its athletes’ advantage.

Archery, badminton, hockey, shooting and squash are all expected to return. Kabaddi, which gets an audience of over 200 million on Indian television, is making its case too. There have even been reports of competitive yoga.

“There will be a discussion around which indigenous sports we want to showcase,” said Raghuram Iyer, chief executive of the Indian Olympic Association.

“When it comes to cricket, we need to have discussions with the ICC because October is a very busy period of the season. It’s part of the Olympics now, and we’d like it at the Games.”

open image in gallery The Commonwealth Games came to a spectacular end ( PA )

A final decision on the sports programme for 2030 is expected to be announced early next year at Commonwealth Sport’s annual general meeting.

To borrow an oft-quoted phrase, reports of the death of the Commonwealth Games have long been greatly exaggerated. But they have never come closer to extinction than when Victoria announced, just two years out, that it no longer wanted to host them.

This sporting alliance of nations, forged from the pink bits of a long-yellowing world order, has never been more precarious. But the Games survived; the decisions that come next will determine whether they thrive.

Fewer sports but no less passion. Different, but not necessarily worse. Comparisons in sport are always difficult, but Glasgow 2026 offered a blueprint for future hosts, showing the “Commies” can still work when budgets don’t.

And they delivered sporting moments too – Josh Kerr’s mile gold, Jamaica’s Sunshine Girls stunning Australia in netball, “Dolphins” domination at the pool, a buzzer-beater in the basketball and the undiluted courage of Archie Goodburn. And bowls, just so much bowls.

open image in gallery Simple Minds headlined the closing ceremony in Glasgow ( PA Wire )

When organisers booked Simple Minds for the closing ceremony, perhaps they knew something we didn’t.

Alive? Yes. Kicking? Not quite.

The Games escaped extinction in Glasgow. Their next chapter will reveal whether survival was merely enough, or the start of renewal.

The race for the Ballon d’Or is entering its final stretch after the world’s best players made significant statements during the 2026 World Cup.

Eight-time winner Lionel Messi showed that, at 39, he could still force himself into the conversation, firing eight goals to propel Argentina to the final and briefly take the crown as the competition’s all-time top goalscorer - until he was eclipsed by Kylian Mbappe.

However, Spain’s triumph over Argentina in the finale will surely bode well for the likes of 2024 winner Rodri and Lamine Yamal in their pursuit of the individual accolade, who will look to start the new club season with some spellbinding performances to complement their part in winning football’s most coveted trophy.

Harry Kane was the favourite for the Ballon d’Or before this summer after his sublime goalscoring campaign with Bayern Munich - can he replicate that unparalleled form in the early months of 2026/27 to make team achievements irrelevant come October’s ceremony?

Here’s how the top 10 front-runners stack up in The Independent’s Ballon d’Or 2026 power rankings:

10. Vinicius Jr

open image in gallery Vinicius Jr could be on the move to Arsenal this summer ( PA Wire )

Vinicius squeezes into our Ballon d’Or power rankings, mainly to spare myself some angry emails from those affiliated to Real Madrid, Brazil, and now maybe Arsenal. I joke, kind of.

The 2024 runner-up had another strong season at the Bernabeu, netting 22 goals in 36 appearances, though like Mbappe was unable to inspire the club to a trophy.

Similar could be said about his World Cup; he was one of the few bright lights in a wooden Brazil side under Carlo Ancelotti, which eventually succumbed to Haaland and co.

Could a move to the Emirates spark life into his Ballon d’Or bid?

9. Michael Olise

open image in gallery Michael Olise has proved himself as one of the world’s best attackers ( Getty )

Crystal Palace could only keep him in Croydon for so long.

With Bayern Munich and France, Olise has established himself as one of the world’s best attackers, a talent so bright that the German giants are doing all they can to ward off interest from the likes of Real Madrid - who no doubt saw the World Cup partnership he formed with Mbappe and want to reunite the pair in the Spanish capital.

Will his electrifying performances be enough to win the Ballon d’Or? Probably not, this year. But he’s in the conversation, which is a statement in itself.

For unrivalled football insight from Miguel Delaney, join Inside Football here.

8. Jude Bellingham

open image in gallery Jude Bellingham silenced his critics at the World Cup ( Reuters )

How was this man’s place on the England plane ever in question?! Thomas Tuchel’s player of the tournament, Bellingham served his critics a serious helping of humble pie by guiding the Three Lions to the elusive World Cup bronze.

That beautiful redemption arc, on its own, has Bellingham on this list. That’s because the season that preceded the World Cup wasn’t spectacular. Injuries limited him to just 13 goal contributions for Real Madrid in another trophyless campaign.

It’s why his chances of winning the Ballon d’Or are still low compared to the competition. But as was proved in North America - don’t count him out.

7. Erling Haaland

open image in gallery Erling Haaland ripped open defences on his World Cup debut ( Getty )

He had us all doing the row.

Their first World Cup since 1998, Haaland ensured Norway lived up to their dark-horse status by powering them to the last-eight. On the way, his unrelenting goalscoring exploits humbled Brazil, sending the five-time winners packing. Away from the big-hitting nations, Haaland was far and away the tournament’s standout player, to little surprise.

Add that to a pretty bog-standard Haaland season for City - just the 38 goals last year, the fourth season he’s hit 30+ at the Etihad - which saw him lift a domestic double. Legacy-defining stats for nearly anyone else, but normal service for the big Norwegian.

As prolific as he may be, he’s currently a definite outsider in the Ballon d’Or race. That may change if he emulates the start to the season he had last year, which saw him smack home 13 in his first 10 league outings. Recency bias can be a powerful thing...

6. Ousmane Dembele

open image in gallery Ousmane Dembele won back-to-back Champions Leagues with PSG ( PA )

Had France won the World Cup, as many expected them to do leading up to that drab semi-final exit, Dembele would have been heavily favoured to secure a second successive Ballon d’Or. The combination of World Cup and Champions League winners’ medals is a bit of a cheat code.

That would’ve been quite the gimme for a player who, let’s be honest, was France’s fourth best attacker at the World Cup. And while, like last year, he ended the season as Paris Saint-Germain’s top scorer with a Ligue 1 and Champions League to boot, he only managed about half of his goalscoring output.

His trophy haul still carries enough weight to be comfortably in the top 10 contenders, but the failure to lift that World Cup title gives him only an outside chance to go back-to-back - and we think that’s fair.

Sorry Ousmane, but this year shouldn’t be your year.

5. Lionel Messi

open image in gallery Lionel Messi, 39, is still in the mix after a stunning World Cup ( PA Wire )

He couldn’t again, could he? Messi’s inclusion on this list encapsulates the significance of the World Cup in deciding the Ballon d’Or winner; he’s not going to take the accolade for his MLS exploits, is he. But fair play to the eight-time winner; at 39, he showed he very much still had it.

Messi’s eight goals propelled Argentina to the World Cup final, where they were rightly defeated by Spain - had he lifted back-to-back titles, he’d probably be towards the top two of this list. After all, he claimed the 2023 award after La Albiceleste’s triumph 10 months earlier, by which time he was on the books at Inter Miami.

Even with his runners-up medal, Indy Sport writers had him as the player of the tournament. That, combined with the jury’s historic love for the Argentinian, means you can’t exactly write him off.

4. Kylian Mbappe

open image in gallery Kylian Mbappe became the World Cup’s all-time record goalscorer this summer ( Reuters )

It feels pretty crazy to think that, at 27, Mbappe still doesn’t have a Ballon d’Or to his name, given he’s been at the top of the game for what feels like forever now.

Once again, he’s very much in the mix this time around. His Golden Boot at the World Cup will do most of the heavy lifting, with his 10 goals in North America seeing him pass first Miroslav Klose and then Lionel Messi as the tournament’s all-time record goalscorer. Both he and Messi would have felt hard done by not to go home with the Golden Ball.

But lest we forget, despite the toxicity that surrounded his club season with Real Madrid, he didn’t exactly experience a drop-off in performance. He bagged 42 goals in 44 games, all while being hounded at the Bernabeu - and while it wasn’t enough to prevent another trophyless season for Los Blancos, you can’t knock his output.

If he can get along with Jose Mourinho and get 2026/27 off to a flyer, he could well shoot up to the pinnacle of these rankings.

3. Lamine Yamal

open image in gallery Lamine Yamal has now won both a European Championship and World Cup before turning 20 ( PA )

And back to the World Cup superiority complex we go, sort of. Yamal will surely win his fair share of Ballon d’Ors across his career, but the 19-year-old could very well end up taking home his first this year, going one better than his runners-up finish in 2025.

Yamal became the first player under 20 to appear at both a European Championship final and a World Cup final - he won both. While his output was pretty modest for his standards, he was influential throughout the tournament for Spain - and that’s after coming into it carrying a hamstring injury.

He also bagged 24 goals and 18 assists across all competitions for Barcelona in another LaLiga-winning season - hardly a mediocre year for the teenager. He’s more than in with a shout.

2. Harry Kane

open image in gallery Harry Kane scored 61 goals in 51 games for Bayern last term ( Getty )

England captain Kane is still the odds-on favourite to win the Ballon d’Or despite failing to set the World Cup alight quite like he managed the Bundesliga in 2025/26. That’s a testament to just how prolific he was last term.

Kane was the top goalscorer in Europe, hitting 61 goals in 51 games across all competitions as he spearheaded Bayern towards the league and cup double; he’s added silverware to his ever-present individual numbers. He was then hardly irrelevant at the World Cup, scoring six goals - including a crucial late brace against DR Congo to spare his country serious embarrassment - as England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966.

If his club form continues into the new campaign, the jury may have to put their emphasis on the World Cup and wider team achievement to one side.

1. Rodri

open image in gallery Rodri won the Golden Ball at the World Cup to stamp his mark on the Ballon d’Or race ( AP )

You might not like it, but the weight of the World Cup in the eyes of the Ballon d’Or jury is undeniable. Just ask Luka Modric.

Rodri had a sensational World Cup at the heart of Spain’s midfield, shielding their rock-solid defence while acting as the metronome that took play forward. His influence took him to the Golden Ball ahead of top goalscorers Messi and Mbappe - and we feel like that could be the precursor to him bringing home a second Ballon d’Or in October.

That would feel like a bit of an injustice, considering he didn’t have the most spectacular domestic season. Returning from injury with Manchester City, it took him a while to properly find his feet in a campaign that saw Pep Guardiola’s side win the FA Cup and League Cup, but miss out on the Premier League title. But the World Cup is the World Cup - and whether you agree with the importance of team achievements in an individual award, the reality is that it does matter a hell of a lot.

His pursuit of a second crown in three years could hinge on his recovery from minor back surgery, and then a possible move to Real Madrid. If he carries his World Cup form and inspires a lightning start to the season at the Santiago Bernabeu, that spotlight could be what swings the jury in his favour.

News.title: A SpaceX rocket is about to smash into the Moon
News.content:

An abandoned SpaceX rocket is about to crash into the Moon.

The spacecraft will hit the lunar surface on Wednesday, around 7.28am UK time, or 2.28am on the east coast. When it does, it will collide with the force of three tons of TNT, leaving behind a hole in the lunar surface and sending pieces of the Moon flying into the air.

Scientists are excited for the opportunities to study that dust and rubble, and see what it might tell us about the composition and nature of the Moon. But experts also warn that the collision is a reminder of the fact that we are filling the space above us with debris and spacecraft that are becoming increasingly dangerous.

The collision will happen near the Moon’s Einstein Creator, on its western edge. It will hit at a speed of about 5,400mph.

The crash will cause an explosive flash, which will not be visible with the naked eye but is expected to be seen with telescopes. It will also throw up a trail of dust and debris that should be visible from Earth, and is likely to stay around for tens of minutes because of the relative lack of gravity and wind to pull it around or blow it away.

After the collision is over, it will leave behind a crater roughly 27 metres across and 5 metres deep. That is not large enough to be seen by Earth, but can be examined with spacecraft.

The collision itself will also be watched by other spacecraft. Nasa’s Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter and South Korea’s Danuri spacecraft – both currently in orbit around the Moon – will be able to gather before and after pictures from the collision, with the latter passing nearby the collision point just two minutes before it happens.

The piece of SpaceX rocket carried two lunar landers and scientific instruments to the Moon in January 2025. It was not intended to crash into the surface.

But it has been floating in space since, and SpaceX has been unable to stop it from colliding with the surface. It is about 12 metres long and weighs around 4,500 kilograms.

It is the second time that a dead rocket has crashed into the Moon by accident. A piece of a Chinese spacecraft left behind two craters on the lunar far side in 2022.

The Moon is regularly hit by meteoroids and other natural objects, and is not protected from them in the way the Earth is by its atmosphere. But those natural objects are unpredictable, and so this offers a rare opportunity for scientists to watch a strike closely.

That is likely to prove useful in the years to come, as Nasa and other space agencies aim to go back to the Moon and perhaps even live on it. Collisions such as these give scientists important data on how the lunar dust might behave, and how safe future astronauts might be from collisions – either with natural objects or space debris.

News.content:

The Russian Embassy in Rome on Monday blamed Ukraine for a deadly weekend bombing at a Moscow restaurant, describing it as an attempt to intimidate the Italian community in Russia.

The embassy said “Kyiv terrorists” wanted to “scare the Italians working in Russia and to show them that they too are in the crosshairs and could become the scoundrels' next victims.”

It said the Saturday night attack on the Balzi Rossi restaurant killed five and injured 19, adding that its Italian chef and his staff were unhurt only thanks to a Russian security guard's “vigilance and selfless dedication to his professional duty.”

There was no immediate comment from Ukrainian authorities.

The National Anti-Terrorism Committee, which coordinates various security agencies, initially reported a lower death toll in a statement issued shortly after the attack. It said the bomb killed three people, including a woman who carried the explosive device into the restaurant, a guard who stopped her, and a guest inside. It said 21 others were injured when the bomb detonated near the restaurant's entrance.

The committee didn’t say who was the target or name the mastermind.

Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin on Sunday described the bombing as a “brutal terrorist act,” but did not say who was responsible for the blast at the upscale restaurant, which is located on the ground floor of a high-rise apartment building that is one of seven skyscrapers in the city that date to the era of Soviet dictator Josef Stalin.

The Russian Foreign Ministry did not respond to a request for comment on the embassy’s statement or explain the higher death toll. The ministry did not issue its own statement on the incident.

Several Russian media outlets claimed the bombing targeted a Russian general who was celebrating his birthday at the restaurant. Some claimed that the general was Col.-Gen. Alexander Chaiko, who recently was appointed the chief of Russia's aerospace forces. The claims could not be independently verified.

Russia blamed Ukraine for past attacks on military officials

Russian authorities have blamed Kyiv for a series of bombings and other attacks against senior military officials after Moscow sent troops into Ukraine in February 2022. Earlier this year, Russia’s Federal Security Service said authorities would tighten security around senior military and government officials following the attacks.

In February, Lt. Gen. Vladimir Alexeyev, ​the deputy head of the GRU ‌military ⁠intelligence service, was shot three times at a Moscow apartment building, but survived. Ukraine denied its involvement.

In December, a car bomb killed Lt. Gen. Fanil Sarvarov, head of the Operational Training Directorate of the Russian Armed Forces’ General Staff, in southern Moscow. Ukraine refrained from comment.

In April 2025, another car bomb that Moscow blamed on Kyiv killed Lt. Gen. Yaroslav Moskalik, a deputy head of the main operational department in Russia’s General Staff. Ukraine didn't claim the attack but hinted at its involvement.

And in December 2024, a bomb hidden in a scooter killed Lt. Gen. Igor Kirillov, who headed the Russian military’s nuclear, biological and chemical protection forces, one of the few attacks Ukraine openly acknowledged.

Among other prominent victims of bombing attacks in Russia were Daria Dugina, the daughter of influential nationalist thinker Aleksandr Dugin, and Vladlen Tatarsky, a well-known pro-Kremlin military blogger. Kyiv denied involvement in the attack on Dugina, and remained coy about the attack on Tatarsky.

News.title: Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Oil plummets as Trump calls off Iran strikes
News.content:
Oil prices have plunged after Donald Trump called off strikes and said the US and Iran would hold further peace talks.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, sank as much as 9.5pc early on Monday to less than $82 a barrel after the US president said he had halted plans for “disastrous” strikes.

Mr Trump said: “Obviously, they don’t want to be attacked. They knew the extent of the attack because they saw it forming.

“Now what we’re doing is we’re talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon.”

The president said that he had been asked by Iran as well as US partners Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar to hold off on strikes. He halted plans for a massive attack against Iran on Saturday, which he said would have been the biggest since the Second World War.

Mr Trump claimed the sides were on the “perimeter” of a peace deal.

Oil’s sharp fall also sent the cost of government borrowing lower on Monday over hopes that it would ease inflation.

The yield on 10-year UK gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, dropped from 5.05pc to 4.98pc, while the equivalent US bonds dropped from 4.74pc to 4.69pc.

Stock markets in Europe also rose, with the FTSE 100 up 0.2pc, the Cac 40 in Paris up 0.3pc and the Dax in Frankfurt climbing 0.1pc.

Jim Reid, an analyst at Deutsche Bank, said: “The latest around Iran is that hopes have risen over the weekend of a diplomatic off-ramp.”

Oil prices are down markedly from their peak of more than $126 a barrel in April, when prices had surged by 74pc in two months.

However, they remain 14pc higher since the US and Israel began their war with Iran on Feb 28 and climbed as high as $100 in July amid fresh clashes in the Gulf. Monday’s fall means oil is at its lowest since July 13.

Petrol prices hit their highest level since the start of the conflict on Friday, with unleaded up to 160p per litre, according to the RAC.

Petrol is now the most expensive it has been since 2022, when Russia’s invasion of Ukraine sent energy prices surging.

If sustained, the fall in oil prices will provide relief for John Healey, the new Chancellor, who pledged in The Telegraph at the weekend that he would watch out for “any suggestions that customers are being taken for a ride at the pump or the till”.

News.title: Inside the trial for a vaccine to end malaria
News.content:
A small group of brave volunteers were given an experimental vaccine in Oxford this week in a bid to bring to an end the centuries-old scourge of malaria.

“I’m on my second vaccine now. Then I’m due to have my third vaccine soon, and then in November, I’ll be given malaria,” said an upbeat Mike Luciw, a 32-year-old local who works in recruitment.

“The hope is to help find something that could save millions of people.”

There are already two licenced vaccines for malaria but the new Oxford “RH5” shot is not like anything that has come before.

The existing jabs only act against malaria as it moves towards the liver in the early stage of infection, and provide only partial protection.

The new combination vaccine, in contrast, is designed to fight it off both at the liver stage and in the wider bloodstream, effectively knocking it out altogether.

The project is being run by the husband and wife team of Simon Draper, Professor of Vaccinology and Translational Medicine at the University of Oxford, and Professor Angela Minassian, an infectious disease specialist and clinical lead for their malaria programme in Oxford’s Department of Paediatrics.

“The dream for malaria … has been to have these two lines of defence, liver and blood, so if the first line fails, you’ve got a second,” says Prof Draper, who leads on the science.

“Our dream is to have a vaccine that gives over 90 per cent efficacy in African children,” adds Prof Minassian, who heads the clinical trials for the new jab.

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

News.title: Josh Kerr turns ‘race of the century’ into one-sided show of power
News.content:
“It means everything – absolutely incredible,” said Kerr, who joined the rendition of Flower of Scotland before closing his eyes to soak up the moment in a stadium where he had competed as a child in even the shot put.

“To do it in front of a Scottish crowd, where I learned how to race, doesn’t get any better,” he added. “I came here week after week growing up as a kid. This was the championship of my season with the world indoors and going after the record. This was on the calendar before any of that. I think a British crowd deserved more from me and I owed them that.”

Of the tactics compared to his world record, where he had to hold an even pace throughout, Kerr stressed the importance of staying calm and not being tempted into pushing too soon. “London was a big stress, pushing my body to the extreme limit,” he said. “Doing a championship race is a nice clean slate; using your brain instead of your body. It’s how I love to race.

“When you’re running that slow, your job is not to waste energy and I did that. I knew an opportunity would open up. Then it was about staying awake and alive and trying to get some space. felt like I had plenty of gears left in me.”

Kerr had emerged to a huge home ovation and, with the Proclaimers booming out as the runners completed the first two laps, he was content to stay in the pack even as Myers followed. There was then only one brief moment of concern as the runners began gathering themselves during the penultimate lap and Kerr became momentarily boxed in.

News.title: Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid
News.content:
Manchester United 2 Atletico Madrid 1

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

News.title: City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter
News.content:
Manchester City 1 Inter Milan 1; Inter win 3-1 on pens

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

News.title: Richarlison grabs last-gasp winner for 10-man Spurs in fiery Chelsea friendly
News.content:
Tottenham Hotspur 2 Chelsea 1

Tottenham concluded their tour Down Under with a 2-1 victory over London rivals Chelsea at Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Sandro Tonali put Tottenham in front with a deflected effort before Estêvão equalised for Chelsea minutes later. Tottenham’s cause was not helped by a red card for Austrian defender Kevin Danso, who lasted just three minutes after coming on at half-time.

After making a mistake, Danso brought João Pedro down and was given his marching orders for denying a clear goal-scoring opportunity. Chelsea came close to taking the lead with their one-man advantage only for Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky to make some crucial saves.



Just as the game appeared to be heading to penalties, Richarlison scored on the follow-up after Jamie Donley hit the post in the final few seconds of added time.

Sports.title: Man Utd legend Paul Scholes’ daughter stuns as she shows off major underboob in tiny bikini
Sports.content:
PAUL SCHOLES’ daughter Alicia has stunned on holiday in a tiny bikini.

The brunette showed off her dazzling body in light blue swimwear, posing in front of a mirror and for selfies.



Netball ace Alicia, who plays for the London Pulse and England, kneeled on a rug in her Portugal summer apartment.

She uploaded pics to Instagram highlighting major underboob as she chilled out.





Alicia, 25, has been away with partner Ayomi Odukoya in Lagos.

The pair have posted snaps from their break with fans loving the content.

One labelled Alicia as a “gorgeous goddess.”

Another said: “pretty girlie”.



Ayomi was a Love Island contender and had a splash on the beach with his sporty Wag.

Alicia is in photos with a football at her feet on the beach and was recorded doing kick-ups with her BF.



Another vid catches her practicing gymnastics by the sea with a set of cartwheels.

Alicia also went out on a speedboat trip and tanned next to their pool.

Sports.title: Man Utd get triple injury boost after Lisandro Martinez World Cup final scare and Sesko missing first three friendlies
Sports.content:
LISANDRO MARTINEZ and Benjamin Sesko are both set to be fit for the start of the season for Manchester United.

Martinez sustained a thigh injury in Argentina’s World Cup final defeat to Spain but it is not a severe setback.



The five-week gap between the final and United’s first Premier League fixture at Hull City has left club medical staff confident that Martinez will have recovered by then.

Martinez’s relatively late arrival and United’s options at centre back could see the 28-year-old eased back into the side.



Michael Carrick has settled on a right-footed-left-footed partnership of Harry Maguire and Ayden Heaven while Leny Yoro has shifted to right back in United’s three pre-season friendlies so far.

Sesko has sat out all three games but his rehabilitation from a shin injury is on track.



The 23-year-old started outdoor training last week and is scheduled to participate in team sessions this week.

Matthijs de Ligt’s own recovery from back surgery is also on track but he will miss the start of the season.

The Dutchman has been missing since November, and underwent surgery on a back injury in May.

United also expected new goalkeeper recruit Karl Darlow to be absent for the first half of pre-season after undergoing a procedure in June.



Darlow, 35, has not done any goalkeeping training since he joined United on a free three weeks ago.

United travel straight from Gothenburg, where they face Paris Saint-Germain on Saturday, to Dublin for a six-day training camp when their full squad will assemble.

Martinez, Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford are due to link up with their teammates in the Republic of Ireland.

Bruno Fernandes, Diogo Dalot, Matheus Cunha and Noussair Mazraoui will report for pre-season training on Monday.

Sports.title: Argentina thug Leandro Paredes booked for classless act just weeks after World Cup final ‘punch’
Sports.content:
LEANDRO PAREDES has landed himself in hot water again after being booked for another classless act during Boca Juniors’ latest match.

The thuggishArgentina midfielder has become notorious for letting his temper boil over and this latest incident is only likely to add to his unwanted reputation.



With an opponent already tumbling to the turf, Paredes lashed the ball straight at the falling player, sparking angry scenes on the pitch.

The referee immediately reached for his pocket and showed the former Roma and Paris Saint-Germain star a yellow card for his actions.



The incident quickly went viral online, with fans slamming the midfielder’s behaviour.

One supporter wrote: “He never learns.”

Another fumed: “How is he always involved in something like this?”

A third posted: “Typical Paredes.”

While one added: “The easiest yellow card you’ll ever see.”

It comes just weeks after Paredes was at the centre of the heated bust-up following Argentina’s World Cup final defeat to Spain.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The midfielder lost his cool at the final whistle as he became embroiled in a confrontation with several Spain players, with chaotic scenes breaking out after Argentina’s 1-0 defeat.

Reports from the aftermath alleged he threw a punch during the melee, while team-mates Nahuel Molina and Nicolas Otamendi were also involved in a fiery confrontation with Rodri.

But this is far from the first time Paredes has made headlines for all the wrong reasons.

Back in the 2022 World Cup quarter-final against the Netherlands, Paredes sparked one of the tournament’s biggest flashpoints.



After flying into a reckless challenge on Nathan Ake, the midfielder then smashed the ball into the Dutch dugout, triggering a mass confrontation involving players and coaching staff.

Virgil van Dijk charged into Paredes, sending him sprawling as tempers boiled over, with many believing the Argentine was fortunate not to be sent off.

Paredes also endured a remarkable collapse while playing for Roma against Genoa in May 2024.



Already frustrated, he was shown two yellow cards in the space of seconds after repeatedly arguing with the referee, earning himself an early walk down the tunnel.

The latest booking will do little to shake Paredes’ reputation as one of football‘s most combustible midfielders.

Despite his undeniable quality on the ball, the 32-year-old continues to divide opinion with his fiery temperament and his latest moment of madness has once again left fans questioning whether he will ever learn.

Sports.title: Incredible moment aggressive PARROT attacks footballers in U15s match forcing referee to stop match
Sports.content:
A BRAZILIAN club was left feeling sick as a parrot … after one of the feathered creatures attacked their players during a cup-tie defeat.

High-flying Rio de Janeiro giants Flamengo took on Ceara in the Brazil Under-15 Cup on Saturday.



But a huge blue parrot invaded the pitch after 17 minutes, swooping onto a Flamengo defender and causing the panicked player to fall to the turf.

The colourful bird menaced several other players, forcing the referee to stop the game before it flew off.



But it returned a quarter of an hour later, perching on the pitch and leading to another holdup in play.

Flamengo overcame the attack to soar into a 1-0 lead – only for Ceara to eventually rule the roost with goals from Andre Luis and Kayck Para.



Ceara held on to secure a 2-1 win, but Flamengo might feel aggrieved after the unusual disturbance.

The unexpected visitor was a blue and yellow macaw, a species that are commonly sighted in South America.

The Rio club could now be tempted into joining the chase for ex-Tottenham striker Troy Parrott.

The Republic of Ireland international is wanted by Fulham and West Ham following two impressive seasons with Dutch club AZ Alkmaar.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

This is not the first time a football game has been interrupted by a bird this year.

In February, a seagull was accidentally knocked out of the sky during an amateur game in Turkey.

Istanbul Yurdum were playing a promotion-deciding game against rivals Mevlanakapi Guzelhisar when the bird was hit during a defensive free kick.

The seagull immediately dropped to the ground as players rushed over to its aid.



Istanbul Yurdum captain Gani Catan was the first to check on the bird and immediately started performing CPR.

He was later seen picking it up and carrying it onto the sidelines for further treatment.

Sports.title: Inside the luxury £300MILLION Airbus private jet Chelsea are chartering around world with 100 beds and sleek living area
Sports.content:
FROM London to Australia to Asia and then back again, Chelsea are not doing this pre-season by halves.

Their players and staff will have flown about 25,000 miles by the time they return home.



But they have not exactly been slumming it.

SunSport can reveal that Stamford Bridge bosses have forked out megabucks to charter one of the top private jets on the market.



An Airbus A340 300 can transport 100 passengers in extreme comfort, carry 1,000 bags and fly non-stop for up to 16 hours.

And to top it all off, they have gone for the VVIP edition.



Machinery that can ferry an entire team about at 540mph is never going to be cheap.

But a brand new jumbo jet with that spec would set you back somewhere in the region of £300MILLION.

Throw in eight flight attendants, a sleek living area and comfy seats that fold flat into beds, and it is clear that this Chelsea mob is travelling in absolute luxury.

It would cost an estimated £400,000 to charter the jet just for the Australia to Hong Kong leg of the journey, which Chelsea completed over the weekend.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



The Blues used the same plane to take them from Gatwick to Sydney, where they played pre-season friendlies against Western Sydney Wanderers and Tottenham.

It is not yet clear whether they will stick with the same equipment to take them on to Indonesia, Malaysia and then back home.

The Airbus A340 300 is the biggest jet in AirX’s private fleet.

They write on their company website: “This jet is perfect for travelling sports teams or musicians who want to safely and comfortably accommodate a large entourage and crew.

“A jet of this size requires ample co-ordination and planning, so we operate with a minimum of 8 cabin crew members who are on hand to attend to all of our passengers’ needs and requirements.



“Our team are adept at tailoring their service, from providing simple snacks and beverages to lavish VIP-style meals.

“The wide body dual-aisle cabin includes 100 lie flat seats that can also easily configured into beds, with pyjamas and other amenities available to ensure a restful journey.”

The next instalment in Chelsea’s pre-season tour is a heavyweight clash with Juventus in Kowloon on Wednesday.

They then face AC Milan in Jakarta three days later and local team Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia the following day before returning to Stamford Bridge for a final warm-up against Real Sociedad.

Xabi Alonso‘s side should then be well limbered up for their Premier League opener at Fulham on August 24.
