Sports.title: Premier League cult hero Charlie Austin ‘gutted’ as he is snubbed for coaching role at former club
Sports.content:
PREMIER LEAGUE cult hero Charlie Austin shared his disappointment after missing out on a coaching role with his former outfit.

The 37-year-old enjoyed a 19-year career as a forward which took him to the Prem and across the EFL.



Among his most notable spells were Burnley and Southampton, going on to make 111 Prem appearances and 218 in the Championship.

But it was Queens Park Rangers where he played more than anywhere else, across two stints in London.



He hoped to make a return to the club in a coaching role after finally hanging up the boots, but has now spoken out revealing he didn’t make the cut in the end.

He wrote on X: “First job interview disappointment.

“Gutted not to progress to the next stage for QPR Academy coaching team. The club I really wanted to work with. Will keep working hard and hoping my time will come

“Good luck to whoever lands the role, what a club you get to join!”

When one critic accused him of making the post for attention, Austin hit back with a classy reply, writing: “No hidden agenda. Just honest disappointment at missing out on a role at a club I think highly of.

“Nothing but respect for QPR, the process was fair and professional, everyone was great.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“As I said will keep working hard for my time to come! This just weren’t my time.”

Austin scored 61 times across 148 total appearances for the Rs, during spells from 2013-16 and 2021-2022.

After leaving the second time he ended up heading abroad to join Brisbane Roar.

But he returned after just seven appearances and bounced around non-league for a number of years before stepping away from the professional game.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino is FINISHED as FIFA president - and it's time for one of game's greats to step up
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino is FINISHED as FIFA president - and it's time for one of game's greats to step up

Gianni Infantino's days in office are almost certainly numbered but there are no ex-players expected to put themselves forward when an election to find his successor takes place

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino is clinging on to power but his days as FIFA president are almost certainly over (Image: Getty Images)

When Gianni Infantino became president of FIFA in February, 2016, the previous incumbent sent a message. “I congratulate Gianni Infantino sincerely and warmly on his election as the new president,” wrote Sepp Blatter. "With his experience, expertise, strategic and diplomatic skills, he has all the qualities to continue my work.”

‌



You were not wrong, Sepp. He has continued your rotten work … and then some. Thankfully, Infantino’s work is now done.

‌



There is surely no scenario imaginable in which he can continue in his role. It is now just a question of how and when he goes. And it then becomes a question of who succeeds Infantino, the man whose rise to the role was greeted with widespread positivity over a decade ago.

‌



Gianni Infantino was set to earn huge salary from World Cup plan as staggering figure revealed READ MORE :

English FA follow Wales in withdrawing Gianni Infantino support after botched World Cup plot READ MORE :

“He is not a politician and he is not an ego,” said Greg Dyke, the chairman of the Football Association at the time. “FIFA has been dominated by egos for a very long time. He is the type of person who will just get on with the job.”

Don’t worry, Greg, you were not alone in being spectacularly wrong. The problem was that everyone in football was in ABB mode. Anyone But Blatter.

The same will probably be true when candidates line up to follow Infantino. The favourite for the job is Victor Montagliani, the 60-year-old Canadian who is currently the president of CONCACAF.

‌



Mattias Granstrom, FIFA’s Swedish general secretary, is very well-respected in the organisation while Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa, the Asian Confederation’s president since 2013, was the candidate narrowly beaten by Infantino in 2016. These potential successors are all highly thought of in football governance circles but then so was Infantino when he took over.

View 3 Images Luis Figo once stood to be FIFA president before pulling out of the race in 2015 (Image: Getty Images)

And do not forget, Infantino still had overwhelming support from member associations right up to his scarcely believable World Cup sell-off scheme. Which surely invites doubt about whether FIFA should be run by one autocratic, football administrator. It should not.

‌



One of the positive things Infantino did was promote the FIFA Legends scheme. For a lot of the time, you felt he only did it so he could play football with famous ex-players - and sit next to them at matches - but, all the same, it is always nice to see greats of the game involved in its promotion.

Greats of the game have been involved in its administration down the years - with mixed results, it has to be said. Most notably, Michel Platini’s presidency of UEFA ended in scandal.

But the world game does not need an autocrat, an executive whose political acumen can force through unwelcome changes. The world game needs a figurehead.

‌



It needs someone who does not need the extra fame. Or the extra money, even. The organisation can be done by committee, of which FIFA has many.

View 3 Images CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani is one of the leading contenders to replace Gianni Infantino (Image: Elizabeth Ruiz Ruiz/Getty Images)

It needs a leader who is emblematic of the sport, rather than a schmoozer, a mover and shaker who wants to court the rich, powerful and famous. It does need a lawyer or a PR man or woman.

‌



When Blatter was elected for a fifth term in May, 2015, Luis Figo had originally planned to stand. He withdrew late in the contest but, for a while, he was an interesting candidate.

And he still would be, along with a whole raft of ex-players - both male and female - with a global standing. Perhaps Sir David Beckham might want to put his hand up.

But seriously, Infantino needs to go and the role needs to change. World football does not need an administrator who can become intoxicated by power - it needs a figurehead who represents everything good about the game.

Sports.title: Leandro Paredes sparks uproar for unsportsmanlike act weeks after World Cup final ‘punch’
Sports.content:
Leandro Paredes sparks uproar for unsportsmanlike act weeks after World Cup final ‘punch’

The Argentine midfielder has again been at the centre of controversy while in action for Boca Juniors.

View 3 Images Leandro Paredes was at the centre of another incident for Boca Juniors. (Image: ESPN Sports Center)

Argentina international Leandro Paredes has again caused an uproar after appearing to kick the ball at an opponent. The midfielder was at the centre of controversy in a hostile end to the World Cup final vs Spain.

‌



After the full-time whistle of Spain’s 1-0 extra-time win over Argentina, Paredes was involved in an incident in which he confronted opposition players. TV footage appears to show him throwing punches towards Gavi and throwing him to the ground.

‌



It was claimed at the time that the 32-year-old was shown a red card for the incident, but that has not appeared on FIFA’s website. It has, however, been confirmed that he has been charged by the governing body for the unsavoury scenes and faces a potential ban.

‌



Non-league footballer shown red card after climbing into stands and confronting fan READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino was set to earn huge salary from World Cup plan as staggering figure revealed READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Parades is now back with his club Boco Juniors, with the Argentine league season at the mid-point. He played 14 minutes of the league game vs Central Cordoba on Sunday, despite the short amount of time, he was still involved in controversy.

A clip shared on social media appears to show Paredes kicking the ball straight at an opponent just as he got to his feet after a foul. There is some argument as to whether it was deliberate or just the midfielder trying to clear the ball.

‌



The incident caused a stir on social media, with some fans clear. “This guy should be sanctioned by @FIFAcom He is a cancer in football,” one said. “He kills the game as we know it. Remove this man.”

View 3 Images Leandro Paredes clears the ball onto his opponent (Image: ESPN Sports Center)

A second added: “He needs to be banned from football for a couple of months. Disgusting player.”

‌



“Genuinely top 2 most dislikable footballers all time lmao and then Argentinians play victim to people hating them when it’s fully deserved,” a third said. A fourth added: “Proper thug this guy. Needs banning.”

A second clip from the game emerged that showed Paraedes reacting towards the referee when not given a foul. “He doesn't like it when the same thing is done to him, so he can see how many players he's done the same to, and he doesn't like a taste of his own medicine,” another fan said.

There were, however, some supporters defending him for the first incident.

‌



“The ref hadn't blown the whistle yet. The ball was in play he cleared the ball,” one said. “The player went down and came back up immediately. This is being blown out of proportion imo.”

A second added: “If you watch the video with audio, it’s clear that he cleared the ball before the whistle was blown.”

Paredes has not yet addressed the melee after the World Cup final. Instead, in the days after the game, he took to social media to send a message .

‌



View 3 Images Leandro Paredes has been charged by FIFA due to the incident after the World Cup final. (Image: Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto/Getty Images)

"Thank you, Argentina! I love you today and always. Today, I write with a heavy heart, having been unable to bring our country the joy it so richly deserves,” he wrote.

"But with a chest full of pride for having given everything we had and for flying our flag at the very top once again! Thank you to everyone who was part of this national team.

Article continues below

"To this group of players who gave their all to represent this jersey, fighting for it until the very last second of every match! It was an honour to be part of the best Argentine national team in history."

Sports.title: Fenerbahce ready to 'break bank' for Marcus Rashford transfer after Man Utd U-turn
Sports.content:
Fenerbahce ready to 'break bank' for Marcus Rashford transfer after Man Utd U-turn

Manchester United could yet offer Marcus Rashford a lifeline following Barcelona's decision to not pursue a permanent deal for the England star but he also has suitors in Turkey

View 3 Images Fenerbahce are interested in Marcus Rashford (Image: Steph Chambers/FIFA)

Fenerbahce are ready to 'break the bank' in order to persuade Marcus Rashford to head to Turkey this summer instead of trying to resurrect his Manchester United career.

‌



Rashford spent last season on loan at Barcelona, who had the option to sign the attacker permanently. However, the Spanish giants instead opted to pursue a deal for Rashford's England team-mate, Anthony Gordon, signing the winger from Newcastle for around £69million prior to the World Cup.

‌



With Rashford now resting after helping England finish third in the tournament, the 27-year-old's future is still unclear.

‌



There have been suggestions that the United academy graduate could be reintegrated at Old Trafford under Michael Carrick in a remarkable change of direction from the club. That has not deterred Fenerbahce, however, who have emerged as an ambitious new suitor for Rashford.

Alejandro Garnacho takes brutal swipe at Chelsea immediately after Aston Villa debut READ MORE :

The Sun claim that Rashford features prominently on a three-man transfer shortlist for Fenerbahce, who are eager to bolster their attacking options. Rafael Leao of AC Milan and Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr are also on the Super Lig outfit's radar.

But Rashford's representatives have already been contacted to gauge whether or not he would be interested in attempting to kickstart his career in Turkey.

‌



And they are ready to go all out to secure his signature if Rashford's camp indicates their client would be interested in such a move.

View 3 Images Rashford has not played for Manchester United in nearly two years but could return to training with them (Image: Getty Images)

Rashford enjoyed a successful loan spell with Barcelona last season with their manager, Hansi Flick, admitting he will miss working with the England star last week.

‌



“You never know what happens with players who are on loan. Our situation is not easy in that respect,” Flick said after a pre-season friendly with Preston North End.

“But I appreciated working with him. He is a fantastic player and a fantastic person. The team will miss him, I will miss him, but that’s life.

“This is something we have to accept. In the end, Anthony Gordon came in and from my first conversation with him, it was clear he was excited to join Barca. I’m really happy he’s on our team.”

‌



View 3 Images Mohamed Salah has also been linked with a lucrative move to Turkey (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista, Getty Images)

Intriguingly, Rashford is not the only high-profile star being pursued by ambitious Turkish clubs this summer with Mohamed Salah also fielding offers from some of the nation's big-hitters.

It seemed as though Besiktas were in pole position to snap up the Liverpool icon on a free transfer, however, it now seems talks have stalled with Trabzonspor making a move for the prolific Egypt star.

Sports.title: Arsenal receive immediate response after finally submitting first Bruno Guimaraes offer
Sports.content:
Arsenal receive immediate response after finally submitting first Bruno Guimaraes offer

Arsenal transfer news as the Gunners finally make an official bid for Newcastle United star Bruno Guimaraes as Mikel Arteta looks to land the midfielder

View 2 Images Arseal's bid has been rejected (Image: Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

Arsenal have seen their opening bid for Newcastle United captain Bruno Guimaraes immediately rejected. The clubs are now in direct talks for the Brazil international.

‌



Guimaraes is due to arrive in La Manga on Monday, where Newcastle's pre-season training camp is based. The midfielder is set for talks with incoming Magpies boss Matthias Jaissle.

‌



Speculation has intensified in recent days over an £80million agreement but it appears the teams are not yet at that stage. It was even suggested that Guimaraes was scheduled for a medical with the Gunners.

‌



However, the 28-year-old departed Brazil on Sunday on a commercial flight, ready to meet up with his Newcastle team-mates. Guimaraes still has two years left on his contract, plus an option for a further year, with the north-east club reluctant to sell.

Newcastle have already secured a £100m fee for Sandro Tonali from Tottenham this summer and sold Anthony Gordon to Barcelona for in the region of £75m. Guimaraes won't arrive at the Emirates cheaply, despite his interest in the move.

Mikel Arteta sends Vinicius Jr transfer message ahead of Real Madrid meeting READ MORE :

Arsenal's initial valuation of Guimaraes is said to have been in the region of £70m. Newcastle are believed to be looking for more than £80m.

‌



Further bids are expected from the north London side after falling short with their first offer. Only Arsenal are said to be in the frame.

Mikel Arteta has discussed Arsenal's ambitions during the transfer window, with the club linked to Vinicius Junior in addition to Guimaraes. The Gunners are set for a busy end to the transfer window.

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes is heading to the exit at Newcastle (Image: Getty Images)

‌

“A lot is happening. We all know about the context of this transfer window," he said.

"From ownership to the board, the sporting director and myself, we know that we want to take this club to a different level. That is going to require a better squad, better individuals.

Sports.title: Non-league footballer shown red card after climbing into stands and confronting fan
Sports.content:
Non-league footballer shown red card after climbing into stands and confronting fan

The incident occurred in the dying minutes of the Scottish Cup preliminary round clash

View 3 Images The Hawick midfielder confronted the jeering fan (Image: X/LeagueDevotion)

Hawick star Paul Tansey was sent off after climbing into the stands and confronting a goading fan. The midfielder, who is the brother of ex-Scotland international Leigh Griffiths, was substituted off and then reacted to someone in the crowd.

‌



Video footage uploaded to social media captured the incident during a Scottish Cup clash with Penicuik. With the scores at 1-1, Hansey was walking towards the away side's dugout when he made a beeline for the home end support.

‌



The 40-year-old stripped his top off before jumping over a wall and running up the steps to confront the fan. Two backroom staff were forced to pull him away from the supporter, who laughed in Hansey's face and continued to jeer him.

‌



As he returned to the sidelines, the referee brandished a red card. Despite this sending off, Hawick equalised and sent the clash to extra time.

English FA follow Wales in withdrawing Gianni Infantino support after botched World Cup plot READ MORE :

Daryl Healy scored the winner for Penicuik, putting his side through to the next round of the domestic competition. Hawick boss Kenny Aitchison condemned the midfielder's actions and confirmed it was being dealt with in-house.

‌



Aitchison said: "We’ve had a chat after the game and this morning after everything calmed down. It’s being dealt with internally. The club cannot comment further until the referee’s report comes in and we speak to the player again, that is the due process.

"This is out of character for the Paul we have seen over the last 18 months as a club. We have never had any incident with him and he’s always been a good trainer and he treats staff and younger players well."

Meanwhile Tansey has spent his career in the lower leagues of Scotland, playing for East Fife, Musselburgh Athletic, Newtongrange and Dalkeith.

Sports.title: Celtic learn CL opponents as Brighton discover European route
Sports.content:
Celtic will play Austrian champions LASK for a place in the league phase of the Champions League, while Brighton will face CFR Cluj or Tromso in the Conference League play-off round.

The draws for the Champions League, Europa League and Conference League play-offs were made on Monday, with Rangers, Hearts, Hibernian, Motherwell and Larne also learning their qualifying routes.

Martin O'Neill's Celtic will host the first leg of their tie against LASK on August 18 or 19, with the return fixture on August 25 or 26. The losers of the tie will drop into the league phase of the Europa League.

Brighton, who finished eighth in the Premier League last season, will play Romanian side CFR Cluj or Norwegian club Tromso to decide who will reach the Conference League's league phase.

The tie will be played on August 20 and 27, with Brighton hosting the second leg, either side of their opening game of the season at home to Aston Villa on August 23, live on Sky Sports.

Rangers and Hearts learn Europa League routes

Rangers and Hearts discovered their Europa League play-off opponents, should they win their third-round qualifying ties.

Derek McInnes' Rangers side travel to Poland this week to face Jagiellonia Bialystok on Thursday in the first leg, with the second leg next week.

Should they win, they will play Northern Irish champions Larne or Iberia 1999 of Georgia in the play-offs. The first leg on August 20 would be at Ibrox, with the return tie the following week.

If Larne lose, they will move into the Conference League play-offs and play Lincoln Red Imps or Omonia.

Image: Derek McInnes is searching for his first victory as Rangers manager

Hearts, who dropped into the Europa League after their Champions League exit, have been drawn against AGF Aarhus of Denmark or Sabah of Azerbaijan in the play-off round.

The first leg of that tie would be at Tynecastle Park on August 20, with the return tie on August 27.

However, Wouter Vrancken's side must first get past Benfica in the third-round qualifying tie. They are away in Portugal on Thursday and back at home next week.

Both clubs will be guaranteed another chance at qualifying for a European competition this season, with the Conference League play-off round awaiting if they lose in the third round of the Europa League.

Rangers would play Jablonec or RFS while Hearts would be up against Paide or SK Rapid.

That has resulted in both clubs requesting that their league game between the first and second legs of any potential play-off tie be postponed, meaning Rangers' game against St Mirren and Hearts' trip to Falkirk are both to be rearranged.

Motherwell and Hibs discover Conference League fate

Motherwell will play Bundesliga club Freiburg - last season's Europa League finalists - in the Conference League play-off round if they beat HJK Helsinki.

Alfred Johansson's side visit HJK on Wednesday in the third qualifying round, with the second leg at Fir Park on Thursday August 13.

Hibernian will play IFK Gothenburg or Gent in the Conference League play-off round should they get past KF Shkendija.

Hibs host Shkendija on Thursday with the second leg on August 13 for a place in the play-offs.

The Conference League play-offs take place on August 20 and 27.

Sports.title: Can Mount be the third midfielder Man Utd are looking for?
Sports.content:
"Why go out searching for a midfielder when you've got Mason Mount at home?"

…A perhaps uncomfortable conversation for most Manchester United supporters to have, but that's the question Mount is forcing Michael Carrick and the Carrington training staff to consider.

The 27-year-old has started every game in pre-season for United and has been among their standout performers against Wrexham, Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid.

"It's only pre-season" will be a valid rebuttal for anyone looking to jump on the Mount hype train. Preparations ahead of the new season can often provide a false representation of reality given differences in fitness and the lack of any real competitive edge. Most United fans will be familiar with this testing assessment of performances during this period.

Andreas Pereira, now plying his trade in Brazil, was once dubbed the "pre-season Pirlo" for his assured performances ahead of new seasons. Those same performances failed to emerge come the beginning of the regular campaign.

Putting that to one side, though, what pre-season does offer is an insight into a manager's thinking. And as United fans wait eagerly to discover what Carrick's side will look like ahead of his first full season in charge, Mount's role could be telling.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking in April, Mason Mount revealed his goal of bringing the Premier League back to Old Trafford

The former Chelsea man has slotted seamlessly into a deeper role. His composure on the ball and industry as a No 8 is exactly what United will be looking for in the market. United prioritised a midfield overhaul this summer following the departure of Casemiro and two signings have already been made in that area.

Andrey Santos from Chelsea has already made an impression on fans and United await to see what impact Youri Tielemans can have. However, fully fit ahead of the new campaign, pre-season has provided Mount with an opportunity to pin down a role and it's one he's very much taking.

While he appears a revelation, Mount's deployment deep in a midfield two isn't new under Carrick. Nor is it new for Mount, having played roughly 4,500 mins as a No 8 or No 6 and 7,000 behind the front man.

Image: Mason Mount percentage by position since 2019/20 (2023/24 excluded due to minimal minutes)

Mount started United's final game of last season, a win at Brighton, in that very role alongside Kobbie Mainoo. While there was no obvious defensive-minded midfielder between the two, the pair's technical ability allowed them to dominate Brighton's midfield in a comprehensive display.

The Brighton game was United's first taste of life post-Casemiro, and Carrick's immediate solution was to play Mount. However, another occasion Carrick chose Mainoo and Mount behind Bruno Fernandes was during a 0-0 draw against Sunderland towards the back end of the season, which was less successful. United were lucky to escape the Stadium of Light with a point.

While Casemiro represented a more combative option that United now lack, Carrick has expressed his admiration for Paris Saint-Germain's midfield dynamic in the past and could be eyeing the chance to replicate those relationships at Old Trafford.

At Parc des Princes, on-the-ball mastery is king over industry and tough tackling and it's a core that's been game-changing for the back-to-back Champions League winners. Mount, whose attitude has seemingly allowed him to adapt to many sides, seems prime for that evolution.

Throughout his career, Mount has always emerged as a managerial favourite. It happened under Frank Lampard on loan at Derby County and back at Chelsea. Thomas Tuchel also found a place for Mount in his teams, while Erik ten Hag was eager to bring him to Old Trafford in a deal worth up to £60m and hand him the famed No 7.

That decision still mystifies most onlookers, as, at times, has the transfer in general. However, before even a ball was kicked under Ruben Amorim following Ten Hag's sacking, he was quick to express his "love" for Mount.

Mount seems to have it all going for him, with coaching staff and team-mates alike evidently willing him on to find success as he enters his third season at United. But anyone familiar with Mount will know the issue doesn't solely lie with his role or ability. Mount's issue has been his fitness, and it's plagued him throughout his Old Trafford career.

Since joining United, Mount has missed around 70 matches with injury and has spent 394 days sidelined. But without hoping to tempt fate, there are signs that he can establish himself as a useful tool in United's squad.

With a return to Champions League football awaiting Carrick's side and a desire to avoid the domestic cup disasters of last season, there will be ample chance for Mount to be deployed. Three years on, United may just be getting the midfielder they hoped they'd signed.

Is he like a new signing? Not really, but United do have Mount at home.

Sports.title: USA cricketer Akhilesh Reddy given eight-year ban under anti-corruption code
Sports.content:
USA cricketer Bodugum Akhilesh Reddy has been banned from all cricket for eight years by the ICC after being found guilty of three counts of breaking anti-corruption rules by a tribunal.

Akhilesh Reddy, who has been banned from cricket since November awaiting the hearing, was found guilty of charges relating to match-fixing, soliciting others to fix matches, and destroying evidence that could have been relevant to the investigation.

The ICC says the offences took place during the Abu Dhabi T10 competition.

"USA player Bodugum Akhilesh Reddy has been banned from all cricket for eight years after an ICC Anti-Corruption Tribunal found him guilty of breaching three counts of the ICC Anti-Corruption Code," the ICC said in a statement.

"The charges relate to the Abu Dhabi T10 2025 in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) for which the ICC was appointed by the Emirates Cricket Board (ECB) as the Designated Anti-Corruption Official (DACO).

"The ban is backdated to 21 November 2025, when Reddy was provisionally suspended.

"The Tribunal found Mr Reddy guilty of the following offences under the Code:

"Article 2.1.1 - Attempting to fix, contrive or otherwise influence improperly, or being party to an agreement or effort to fix or contrive in any way or otherwise influence improperly, the result, progress, conduct or other aspect of matches in the ADT10 2025.

"Article 2.1.4 - soliciting, inducing, enticing, instructing, persuading, encouraging or intentionally facilitating (or attempting to do the former) another participant to breach Article 2.1.1 of the Code in one or more matches in the ADT10 2025.

"Article 2.4.7 - Obstructing the DACO's investigation through deletion of data and messages from a mobile device which may have been relevant to the DACO's investigation."

Arsenal's opening bid for Bruno Guimaraes has been rejected by Newcastle.

The Premier League champions are now in direct talks with Newcastle over a deal for their captain.

Guimaraes is in Spain to report back for their pre-season training camp in La Manga.

The 28-year-old told Newcastle bosses last month he wants to join Arsenal this summer.

Newcastle want their captain to stay and he has two years left on his contract plus a club-held option for a third.

Arsenal are now discussing internally whether to go back in with an improved offer.
