World.title: These were the most-watched FIFA World Cup matches in Hungary
World.content:
Never before in the history of the FIFA World Cup have there been as many matches as there were in 2026. A total of 104 matches were played, most of which Hungarian viewers could watch on M4 Sport, while a few matches were broadcast on the Duna World channel due to overlapping events at the end of the group stage. Two weeks after the World Cup, it’s worth looking back at which matches drew the largest audiences, based on viewership data.

The World Cup final was the most-watched program of the year so far

According to data from Nielsen Közönségmérés Kft., the final—in which Spain defeated Argentina 1–0 after extra time—drew an average of 1,502,352 viewers across the entire population via television. This made the broadcast on M4 Sport the most-watched TV program of 2026 so far, at least when considering only linear broadcasts; after all, the event could also be followed online on the M4 Sport website and on Médiaklik. In the case of the online platforms, the public broadcaster reported an audience of 227,000 on the day following the World Cup final.

Interestingly, only two other television programs in Hungary have come close to this figure so far this year. On January 1, TV2 reached 1,468,431 viewers with the film *How Could I Live Without You?*. Many believed even then that no channel would achieve higher viewership than this throughout the year, but ultimately, RTL also came close with its broadcast of the UEFA Champions League final in Budapest. An average of 1,430,219 viewers tuned in to watch the match on television, which is a truly outstanding figure, but it wasn’t quite enough to break the record set up to that point. However, the picture is somewhat nuanced by the fact that many people watched the Champions League final via the RTL+ streaming service; based on linear TV viewership figures, though, we had to wait until the World Cup to reach 1.5 million viewers.

What about the other matches?

As the World Cup heated up, the matches attracted increasing attention. An average of 1,027,898 people across the entire population tuned in to the England-Argentina semifinal, placing the match—broadcast by M4 Sport—in second place on the Week 29 viewership chart, though it also took the bottom spot on the podium that week. The excitement of the bronze medal match between France and England drew 636,658 viewers despite the late start time, so it wasn’t just the fact that the English won 6–4 and a total of 10 goals were scored that piqued so many people’s interest afterward.

However, the bronze medal match still didn’t make the top three when compared to the viewership numbers of other World Cup matches. The round of 16 match between Portugal and Spain was the week’s top-rated game with 937,407 viewers. Behind that, the Spain-Belgium quarterfinal took fourth place on the overall World Cup viewership list (731,277 viewers), while the fifth-most-watched match was the Brazil-Norway clash (647,949 viewers). This round of 16 match proved sufficient for M4 Sport to win the ratings race for the entire 27th week.

In the six weeks since the World Cup began, there was only one instance during the group stage when a non-World Cup match topped the relevant lists. In Week 25, for example, RTL’s and TV2’s news programs both outperformed the live broadcast of the group stage match between Portugal and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The latter was watched by an average of 570,163 viewers across the entire population, but there were matches during the group stage that generated even higher viewership figures.

World.title: Eastern Romania: Iași switches off street lighting after midnight amid energy sector state of alert
World.content:
Iași, a city in northeastern Romania, has decided to reduce its public street lighting following the nationwide state of alert declared in Romania's energy sector on July 31

The street lighting is switched off after 24:00 in the city, except on hospital grounds, underpasses, and busy central areas such as the city’s Union Square, TVR Info reported. The Local Police will deploy additional officers to patrol the streets, Iași mayor Mihai Chirica announced.

According to the mayor, the measure is expected to save around 10 MWh of electricity every night.

Other cities in Romania, namely Tecuci and Botoșani, will introduce similar measures.

The government declared a nationwide state of alert in the energy sector for the entire month of August after severe drought and very low water levels curtailed electricity production.

Meanwhile, state-owned nuclear power producer Nuclearelectrica said that it began importing electricity from Ukraine through Moldova's state-owned energy supplier Energocom to offset the shortfall caused by the shutdown of Unit 1 at the Cernavodă nuclear power plant.

World.title: Investment fund BoldMind, Pall-Ex Romania management team acquire company in deal exceeding EUR 25 million
World.content:
Regional private equity fund BoldMind Capital Partners and the executive management team of Pall-Ex Romania, the Romanian operator of the international Pall-Ex franchise, have completed the acquisition of the palletized freight transport company through a leveraged buy-out (LBO) transaction valued at more than EUR 25 million.

The transaction was financed through equity provided by BoldMind Capital Partners and the management team, complemented by a financing facility from Banca Transilvania.

Pall-Ex Romania was previously part of the international Delamode Group, a specialist in logistics and international freight management.

The new ownership structure will enable the company to accelerate investments, respond more rapidly to market opportunities, and develop new value-added services for both network members and customers, the new owners said.

The company's executive management remains unchanged.

Pall-Ex Romania's growth strategy focuses on strengthening its leadership in its core business, namely palletized freight distribution, while also exploring new development opportunities and expanding its service portfolio, the company said. It aims to leverage the potential of its Romanian partner network while achieving closer operational integration with Pall-Ex partners across other European markets in order to increase cross-border transport volumes.

Last year, Pall-Ex Romania generated revenues exceeding EUR 40 million. Established 15 years ago in Sibiu, Pall-Ex Romania has 120 employees. It brings together nearly 60 member companies and serves more than 11,000 active customers.

"BoldMind's decision to acquire Pall-Ex was based not only on the exceptional quality of the company, which has consistently delivered profitable growth over the past ten years, but also on the motivation, commitment and performance of its management team. The team successfully combines the entrepreneurial mindset of founders building businesses with the discipline and operational rigor typical of major international corporations. At the same time, the attractiveness of palletized freight logistics, one of the fastest-growing segments of the European road freight transport market, was an important factor supporting our investment decision," Dragoș Roșca, Managing Partner at BoldMind Capital Partners, explained.

"We are entering a new phase of development in which we will accelerate investments, digitalization and service expansion. Our objective is for these investments to translate into better services, greater opportunities for our network members and a genuine competitive advantage for our customers. Pall-Ex is committed to remaining Romania's benchmark for palletized freight distribution," Danor Ionescu, Chief Executive Officer of Pall-Ex Romania, said.

BoldMind Capital Partners is a regional private equity firm managing BoldMind Fund I, a EUR 60 million investment fund dedicated to high-growth private companies across Romania, Bulgaria and Croatia.

World.title: Romania's Nuclearelectrica imports electricity from Ukraine as low Danube levels disrupt nuclear output
World.content:
State-owned nuclear power producer Nuclearelectrica said that it began importing electricity from Ukraine through Moldova's state-owned energy supplier Energocom to help offset the loss of generation caused by the shutdown of Unit 1 at the Cernavodă nuclear power plant. The move comes as Romania faces reduced electricity production due to historically low Danube water levels caused by severe drought.

Nuclearelectrica said the imported electricity will help reduce the impact of the loss of Unit 1's output on the Romanian electricity market.

The company explained that the purchase was made with the support of Energocom, with which it signed a memorandum of understanding in 2023 aimed at strengthening energy resilience and mutual support between Romania and the Republic of Moldova.

“The current difficult situation in Romania and across the region, caused by the extremely low water level of the Danube due to severe drought, requires long-term partnerships and strong commercial relations that allow for mutual support and the maintenance of the stability of the National Energy System," Nuclearelectrica said.

Acting prime minister Ilie Bolojan announced late last week that the government declared a nationwide state of alert for the month of August because of reduced electricity production caused by drought and historically low water levels in the Danube and other rivers.

The government has adopted a series of measures aimed at keeping Unit 2 at the Cernavodă nuclear power plant in operation while increasing electricity production from other sources and boosting imports.

Unit 1 at Cernavodă was shut down last week as a preventive measure after the Danube reached exceptionally low levels. Although Nuclearelectrica had warned that Unit 2 might also need to be disconnected, the company announced on July 30 that an overnight technical assessment found the reactor could continue operating safely.

“The operation of Units 1 and 2 of Cernavodă NPP is carried out based on strict monitoring of operating parameters and safety margins, as well as on procedures specific to drought conditions; thus, as long as the analysis of these parameters allows the operation in compliance with all nuclear safety norms, Unit 2 will remain connected to the National Energy System," the company said last Thursday.

Nuclearelectrica cautioned that Unit 2 could still be shut down at any time should Danube water levels decline further and affect the plant's operating conditions.

In related news, the National Institute of Hydrology and Water Management (INHGA) said on July 31 that Danube flows are expected to remain exceptionally low in the coming days, with the river's discharge at the Baziaș entry point forecast to fall to around 1,450 cubic meters per second by August 6. The figure is well below the multiannual averages of 4,700 cubic meters per second for July and 3,900 cubic meters per second for August.

The institute said flows are likely to remain around that level until August 10-12, with a gradual increase expected in the second half of the month, although it cautioned that medium- and long-term forecasts remain highly uncertain under the current severe drought conditions.

World.title: Băile Govora: Romanian spa town’s architectural heritage under the spotlight at August events
World.content:
A series of events taking place this month will allow the public to (re)discover the architectural heritage of the Romanian spa town of Băile Govora, in Vâlcea county.

The Museum of Architecture of Romania (MuzA), the Govora Spa Architecture Days, and the Govora Heritage Lab Summer School celebrate the cultural identity of the historic spa resort through a diverse program of exhibitions, guided tours, film screenings and more.

From August 1 to September 20, the Museum of Architecture of Romania (MuzA) will present the exhibition MuzA at the Spa at Hotel Ștefănescu, one of Govora's landmark buildings, erected in 1902. Curated by IDEILAGRAM Association and produced in partnership with Studiogovora and STOA, the exhibition forms part of MuzA's national project that documents architecture and the relationship between people and place in 11 communities across Romania.

As part of an original installation, Studiogovora invites visitors to rediscover fragments of lost architectural heritage and reflect on the importance of understanding, preserving and revitalizing the buildings that still survive and depend on collective efforts to endure and return to life, the organizers explain.

From August 1 to August 15, the Govora Heritage Lab Summer School runs a program bringing together more than 40 architecture students, who will learn while contributing to the conservation and restoration of Govora's architectural heritage. This year's activities will once again focus on Villa Constanța-Marieta (pictured in opening photo), a historic building more than a century old. Students will restore the villa's original woodwork and decorative veranda elements, continue investigating the building's historical layers, create tactile models of some of Govora's landmark buildings, and develop ideas for improving the town's public spaces.

Held between August 6 and August 9, alongside the summer school, the Govora Spa Architecture Days aim to show how “heritage comes to life when it is explored and experienced collectively.”

"Heritage gives a community and a place its identity, hence what makes the experience unique. If restored and properly showcased, Govora's heritage can help distinguish the town within Romania's spa and cultural tourism market, attracting visitors throughout the year rather than only during the events we organize," architect Radu Tîrcă, president of Studiogovora, explained.

"We have prepared themed guided tours, workshops dedicated to Govora's local heritage, UrbanEye architectural documentary film screenings, and a concert featuring Corina Sîrghi and Cătălin Răducanu. Over time, we hope these activities will inspire a new relationship with the town, one that is more caring, more active, and more open to collaboration," Irina Leca, vice-president of Studiogovora, said.

The full program of events is available on the Studiogovora website.

Founded in 1887, Băile Govora is an example of the influence of French culture on Romania's modernization. The spa town was planned according to urban planning principles inspired by French spa resorts while being adapted to the local context.

Studiogovora is an interdisciplinary collective working to transform the spa heritage of Govora and the wider Oltenia region into a living resource for local communities and future generations.

World.title: Romanian pianist Alexandra Dăriescu makes BBC Proms debut this week
World.content:
Romanian pianist Alexandra Dăriescu will perform at the BBC Proms, the summer classical music festival held annually at Royal Albert Hall and other venues across the United Kingdom, this week.

She is the first Romanian female pianist to perform at the festival, joining a very small group of Romanian pianists to have appeared at the well-known event, namely the late Radu Lupu and Mîndru Katz.

Dăriescu’s concert will take place on August 5, at Royal Albert Hall, alongside the Hallé Orchestra, with Kahchun Wong conducting.

She will perform Fantaisie for Piano and Orchestra by Nadia Boulanger, a work receiving its BBC Proms premiere. The choice of repertoire reflects Dăriescu’s “longstanding commitment to rediscovering and promoting works that remain underrepresented in the international concert repertoire, particularly those by women composers,” a release from the Romanian Cultural Institute (ICR) explains. Throughout her career, she has championed music by Nadia Boulanger, Clara Schumann, Dora Pejačević, Leokadiya Kashperova and Doreen Carwithen, alongside the major works of the piano repertoire.

The program also features Sergei Rachmaninoff's Symphony No. 2 in E minor, Op. 27, as well as Maurice Ravel's La vallée des cloches in an orchestration by Colin Matthews.

Alexandra Dăriescu made her debut in Iași at the age of nine with the National Orchestra of Moldova. At 17, she moved to the UK to study at the Royal Northern College of Music in Manchester. She settled in the UK, becoming a British citizen and establishing an international career.

A major career milestone came with her debut at Royal Albert Hall in 2013. She has performed with leading orchestras including the London Philharmonic Orchestra, London Symphony Orchestra, BBC Symphony Orchestra, Orchestre National de France, Oslo Philharmonic, Royal Stockholm Philharmonic Orchestra and Sydney Symphony Orchestra.

Her advocacy for greater representation of women composers led to the creation of the Alexandra Dăriescu Award at the Leeds International Piano Competition, the first prize of its kind recognizing the performance of a work composed by a woman. In 2017, she created and produced the multimedia performance The Nutcracker and I, combining piano music, dance and digital animation. The production has been staged more than 100 times across Europe, Asia, Australia and the United States.

She has received numerous distinctions, including the title of Cultural Ambassador of Romania, the Order of the Crown of Romania in the rank of Officer, awarded by the Romanian Royal Family, and the Young European Leader distinction from Friends of Europe. In 2020, she was awarded Romania's Order of Cultural Merit in the rank of Knight and became an Associate of the Royal Northern College of Music, where she also taught piano for two years. Since September 2024, she has been a professor of Piano at the Guildhall School of Music & Drama in London.

The 2026 BBC Proms runs from July 17 to September 12, bringing together leading classical musicians from around the world. While most of the festival's 86 concerts take place at Royal Albert Hall in London, this year's edition also includes 14 Proms Across the UK concerts and residencies in Bristol, Gateshead, Middlesbrough, Sunderland and Mold, alongside associated events such as Proms in the Park. Established in 1895 by impresario Robert Newman and conductor Henry Wood as the Henry Wood Promenade Concerts, the festival has been organized and broadcast by the BBC since 1927.

World.title: Snap Elections Remain Uncertain After Serbia’s No-Confidence Vote
World.content:
Last week, a no-confidence vote was held in Serbia’s parliament in the Serbian Progressive Party-led government.

The motion failed. But for the opposition, it was still an opportunity to speak about the government’s affairs, and for experts, another discussion about when potential snap elections could be held.

Sixty-two opposition MPs submitted a request for a no-confidence motion in February. The first parliamentary session with such a motion on the agenda was scheduled for April – but the ruling majority failed to secure a quorum at two sessions held that month.

Until the no-confidence procedure was concluded, the standard legal process for calling snap elections could not begin.

World.title: Greek Arrests Revive Politically Charged Case of 2010 Bank Arson
World.content:
The case was reopened in July, amid unconfirmed claims of an anonymous tip-off sent by email.

“It doesn’t convince me,” Karagianni told Greek MEGA TV on July 11. Calling for “substantial evidence”, Karagianni said: “We want the perpetrators to be exposed and taken to where they should be taken, which is to prison.”

Thrasivoulos Kontaxis, a lawyer representing 11 injured survivors and relatives of the victims, said he was “cautiously optimistic” of justice being served.

“It will represent mental redemption, that at the end of this journey someone was actually called upon to pay the price by being punished, at least.”

Three people died in the bank fire, caused by a trio of black-clad, masked individuals who set fire to the building on central Stadiou Street during a protest against the austerity demanded of Greece.

Bank employees Epaminondas Tsakalis, Paraskevi Zoulias and Angeliki Papathanasopoulou were trapped by the flames on the third floor and suffocated to death. Papathanasopoulou was pregnant. Twenty-one others were injured.

In 2013, three bank executives were convicted of manslaughter and bodily harm due to negligence; two were sentenced to 22 years in prison and the third to five years and one month.

Then, in 2016, two men were charged with arson but acquitted due to a lack of evidence. The case was closed, reopened again in 2020, reportedly following an anonymous phone call, only to be shelved again.

None of the three suspects have been named. All have denied any wrongdoing.

World.title: Croatia’s War Crimes Prosecutions are Stagnating, Watchdog Warns
World.content:
This post is also available in this language: Bos/Hrv/Srp

Bozica Ciboci, Vesna Terselic and Veselinka Kastratovic. Photo: Documenta

Since Croatia joined the European Union, the effectiveness of its war-crimes prosecutions has stagnated while crimes committed against Serbian civilians and prisoners-of-war are almost never investigated, a report presented on Friday by Documenta – the Centre for Dealing with the Past, says.

“The number of proceedings is declining. We have recorded 33 criminal proceedings in the trial phase before county courts, involving a total of 91 defendants,” Documenta head Vesna Terselic said, presenting the 2025 Report on Monitoring Criminal Proceedings for War Crimes.

By comparison, there were 54 criminal proceedings in 2024, 64 the year before, and 61 in 2022.

Of the 91 defendants in war-crimes proceedings in 2025, 87 were members of Serbian paramilitary and police forces. The remaining defendants included three former members of the Croatian Army and one member of the Croatian Defence Council, HVO.

Terselic said many dedicated professionals work in the State Attorney’s Office, the police, the courts and the Ministry of Croatian Veterans, but that county state attorneys’ offices lack the capacity to investigate unresolved war-crimes cases.

“Recently, a final verdict brought to an end one of the longest war crimes trials, in which Branimir Glavas was convicted. That trial would not have happened if witness Krunoslav Fehir had not spoken out. It would not have happened if Vladimir Faber had not investigated the case while serving in the police. It was an extremely difficult crime to investigate, and many institutions failed to support the investigation,” Terselic recalled.

She said recent legislative amendments had improved the position of civilian victims of the 1990s Homeland War, but that changes to the law on the rights of victims of sexual violence during the armed aggression against Croatia were still needed.

“Unfortunately, today, there is not a single active trial for crimes committed during Operations Storm and Operation Flash. No one disputes the right of the Croatian Army and police to liberate occupied parts of Croatia and re-establish state authority there, but no one gave them the right to follow that with criminal acts,” said Veselinka Kastratovic, legal adviser at the Centre for Peace, Nonviolence and Human Rights Osijek.

“We cannot say it did not happen. We all know in Croatia that it happened; some people simply choose to look away,” she added.

Documenta’s report also criticises public statements by some high state officials, saying they reflect “one-sided and simplified interpretations of recent history”.

More positively, the report highlighted the commemoration of the killings in Varivode, where then-President Ivo Josipovic and Prime Minister Andrej Plenkovic delivered messages of remembrance.

In Varivode, Croatian soldiers killed nine elderly Serb civilians after Operation Storm, a key Croatian Army operation in 1995, which overwhelmed a self-proclaimed Serbian statelet on Croatian territory.

Bozica Ciboci of Documenta called on countries across the region to “sign agreements aimed at improving the prosecution of war-crimes perpetrators and preventing the politicisation of war crimes trials.”

World.title: Money the Greatest Challenge Facing Serbia’s Small, Independent Media
World.content:
For Serbia’s small independent newsrooms, pressure comes not only in the form of intimidation, spurious lawsuits, or physical assault. Increasingly, it is financial.

The Serbian media landscape is sharply divided between outlets close to the ruling Serbian Progressive Party, SNS, and independent newsrooms.

Research has found that media loyal to the ruling party are the primary beneficiaries of co-financing and advertising from public bodies. Independent media are starved of such funds.

This helps explain why pro-government outlets can operate without the same financial pressures, while independent newsrooms struggle to cover basic overheads and remain vulnerable to political and economic pressure.

World.title: Is Spending in July in Croatia Really Breaking Records?
World.content:
August the 3rd, 2026 – Tax Authority data for spending in July in Croatia shows continued growth in fiscalised spending, but the nominal figures need to be interpreted with caution.

Higher receipt totals don’t actually necessarily mean that residents and tourists bought more goods and services, because part of the increase comes from higher prices. Index writes that in order to assess the real trend in consumption it is necessary to remove the effect of inflation. When nominal data are adjusted for price rises, the real growth is noticeably weaker, and in some periods and sectors spending stagnates or even falls.

price increases are largely responsible for nominal growth

According to Tax Authority data on fiscalised spending, food-and-beverage preparation and serving activities as well as the accommodation sector in Croatia recorded strong growth during the summer months, with a clear seasonal jump towards July. The cumulative change compared with the previous period is positive, and growth is also visible in the monthly figures.

In food-and-beverage preparation and serving, fiscalised turnover during the month of July reached 891 million euros nominally, or 860 million euros when adjusted for inflation. In the same month last year the turnover stood at 802 million euros. This means the nominal value of receipts increased by around 11 percent, while real growth after removing the effect of higher prices was about 7 percent.

Cumulatively, from the beginning of the year to the end of July, turnover in hospitality was 11 percent higher nominally than in the same period last year. After correction for inflation the real growth stood at 6.5 percent. In other words, guests and residents did spend more than last year, but the difference is not as large as the nominal figures suggest because part of the rise stems from higher prices of food and drink.

a look at accommodation

Results by county are highly uneven. While some counties recorded real growth in fiscalised accommodation turnover of more than 30 percent, others saw double-digit declines. Most Adriatic counties achieved moderate growth, yet even on the coast the results are not uniform. In some counties turnover rose by only a few percent, while Dubrovnik-Neretva County recorded a slight real decline of 0.6 percent.

Extreme results in individual counties should be interpreted cautiously; they may be the consequence of a low comparative base, changes in coverage or local specifics rather than a dramatic shift in overall tourist activity. During July, fiscalised turnover in the accommodation sector reached 691 million euros nominally, compared with 630 million euros in the same month last year – a nominal increase of 9.7 percent. After removing the impact of inflation this year’s turnover amounts to 667 million euros, meaning it was 5.9 percent higher in real terms than in July last year. Guests therefore left almost ten percent more money for accommodation, but the actual growth in consumption was closer to six percent.

was july 2026 really more successful than july 2025?

The data show that fiscalised turnover in July was higher than last year in both hospitality and accommodation, even after adjustment for inflation. Nevertheless, real growth was significantly weaker than the nominal figures, and results vary considerably between sectors and counties.

It can therefore be concluded that July was better than last year’s according to the indicators examined, but not that the season was dramatically or unequivocally more successful. Tax Authority data are currently the most reliable publicly available indicator of fiscalised spending, yet they do not cover every element of the tourist result. An important methodological change should also be noted: from this year the Tax Authority’s reporting includes payments via transaction accounts. In order to keep the data comparable with the previous year, those payments have been excluded from this analysis.

The conclusion is therefore cautious: nominal spending is rising, but once inflation is taken into account the picture is considerably more moderate. The figures show seasonal growth and large regional differences, but they do not unambiguously confirm that this year’s July was significantly more successful.

World.title: Meet Taljurić, The Strange Croatian Fingerprint Island
World.content:
August the 3rd, 2026 – Taljurić, (or Pijat if you’re local) is a strange formation, it’s a totally flat Croatian island that resembles a human fingerprint and has absolutely zero vegetation on it.

The Adriatic might look calm and alluring during summer, but it’s no stranger to surprisingly violent storms and winds. When they hit, the usually calm Adriatic becomes very choppy and washes over almost its entire surface repeatedly. Putni kofer writes that over countless centuries, these repeated actions have made it appear like a flat stone plate laid carefully in the middle of the open, unforgiving sea.

Wherever you look along Croatia’s heavily indented, rugged and island-laden coastline, something takes your breath away. Be it stunning beaches, pebbles and rocks of every shape, secret coves, water shifting from transparent turquoise to deep blue, shores battered by waves on one side and watched over by powerful mountains on the other… The list goes on. Then there are the 1,000+ islands, small and large, bare and green, low and steep, and some of the most unusual shapes imaginable. Some have been inhabited for thousands of years; others hold only a lighthouse, a lonely chapel or traces of former farming. A few are so tiny and exposed that almost nothing can grow on them. Among these rocky outcrops lie some of the strangest sights on the Croatian coast.

From Galešnjak and Baljenac to… Pijat, (Taljurić)

Some of these islands have gained worldwide recognition. Galešnjak, thanks to its almost perfect heart shape, became known as the Island of Love. Baljenac (also called Bavljenac), seen from the air, resembles a giant human fingerprint – an effect created by the dense, tangled network of dry-stone walls that once enclosed tiny agricultural plots. In this sea of bizarre shapes lies another islet whose appearance is perfectly captured by its name. It is called Taljurić (locally also known as Pijat). Viewed from the sea or from the air, it really does look like a large stone plate carefully placed on the surface of the Adriatic.

Taljurić lies within the boundaries of the remarkable Telašćica Nature Park, on the south-eastern part of Dugi otok, and is regarded as one of the most unusual natural phenomena of this protected area. Official documents list it as a rock (hrid) and rank it among the smallest islands and rocks in the park’s archipelago. It measures about 60 metres in diameter and rises only three metres above the sea.

In essence, it is an almost flat stone slab made of horizontally layered limestone. Its upper surface has been continuously exposed to waves, salt and wind, so the whole islet looks as if the sea has been grinding and levelling it for centuries. During powerful storms the waves can sweep across nearly its entire surface – which explains why no vegetation has ever managed to take hold.

no vegetation manages to take hold on taljurić

Its unusual appearance directly influenced its name. The islet resembles a flat, round board of the kind once used in kitchens, which Venetian sailors called “tagliero” in their dialect. According to Telašćica Nature Park, the name Taljurić, which isn’t frequently used by locals, developed from that word. There are absolutely no trees, bushes or grass on the surface. Although from a distance it looks completely barren, its edge is not lifeless. On the rocks just above the waterline live colonies of barnacles (known locally as brambuljci), tiny marine crustaceans that cling tightly to the stone and withstand the constant pounding of the waves.

Another curiosity lies on the south-western side of Pijat: the remains of a former fossil cave whose roof eroded away over geological time. Today it looks like a cave open to the sky – a stone hollow without a ceiling. The sea around the islet is rich in life, and the wider Telašćica area includes valuable marine habitats such as posidonia meadows, underwater cliffs, reefs and sea caves.

World.title: Stari Grad Pag: The Croatian Town That Cholera Forcibly Relocated
World.content:
August the 3rd, 2026 – Stari grad Pag was entirely planned and constructed, but ended up being completely relocated because of a cholera outbreak that decimated the local population.

Stari grad (Old town) Pag used to be quite a large, fairly wealthy town protected by impressive walls, much like those down in Dubrovnik. Putni kofer writes that all was well until 1852, when a terrible cholera epidemic struck and decimated the local population. It was at that point that plans pivoted, and the entire town ended up elsewhere.

stari grad pag – the town that moved

It’s very well known at this point that the moon-like, rather bizarre looking island of Pag offers an otherworldly landscape of stark stone expanses, centuries-old salt pans that still yield “white gold,” outstanding cheese, and a history stretching back to the Middle Ages. Its main town, Pag, is the ideal base for exploring the island. Highlights include the Gradac viewpoint, the historic core reached via the stone Katina bridge, and the remains of walls and towers.

Few people know that the original Pag actually stood roughly one kilometre further south. Residents moved to the present planned town in the 15th century. Old Pag flourished throughout the Middle Ages thanks to salt production, which sustained the island. On the hilly ground next to the salt pans sat churches, monasteries, a fortified citadel, a palace, large and small loggias, a hospital, and large and small town squares. Along the coastline itself stood salt warehouses and two harbours – Veliki and Mali mul. What remains of Old Pag today are the ruins of the Franciscan monastery and the Romanesque Church of St Mary, which houses a wooden Gothic statue of the Mother of God.

salvation from a deadly disease? maybe…

For a century and a half, every year on the Feast of the Assumption (on the 15th of August), the people of Pag make a pilgrimage from the Old Town to the new Pag, carrying with them the statue of the Blessed Virgin Mary. The votive procession dates from 1855 and has a striking historical background.

The devastating cholera epidemic hit Pag hard in 1852 and took a particularly heavy toll. To stop the spread of the disease, all cemeteries were moved out of the town and local churches. On Assumption Day back in 1855, the townsfolk spontaneously gathered around the statue of the Mother of God in the then Stari grad, praying for deliverance. After they carried the statue on their shoulders to Pag’s Collegiate Church, the last cholera victims were buried on the 16th of August, on the feast of St Roch. The residents then vowed that every single year on that day, they would bring the statue to Pag, where it would remain in the Collegiate Church for a full 22 days, until the Nativity of Mary, so the faithful could give thanks and pray for health, peace and love.

the discovery of remarkable megaliths and an ancient greek settlement

Megaliths and numerous artefacts from antiquity have been found on the site of Stari grad Pag, indicating that a human settlement already existed and functioned there way back during ancient Greek times. The old town was once so rich and economically powerful that it could finance the construction of its own defensive walls.

Its history was also shaped by King Béla IV, who, back in 1244, found refuge on the island while fleeing his enemies. In gratitude for the help he received, he granted Pag a charter as a free royal city. After the relocation in the second half of the 15th century, Stari grad Pag lost its importance and eventually ceased to be an independent settlement. Its only fully preserved building is the Church of St Mary, first mentioned in 1192 and believed to stand on the site of an early Croatian basilica from the 8th century. It was saved from ruin by the Franciscans, who built a monastery nearby and lived there from the 16th until the end of the 19th century.

World.title: Dear Tourists: There Are No Private Beaches in Croatia
World.content:
August the 3rd, 2026 – If someone tells you that there are private beaches in Croatia you can’t enter this summer, you can freely ignore them and carry on swimming.

As Index reports, the basic rule is simple: on almost every beach in Croatia you are allowed to swim, sunbathe and spread out your towel – even if the beach is situated in front of a hotel, campsite, apartment complex or private villa. The sea and the seashore form part of the maritime domain in Croatia. That means they are not private property and are intended entirely for public use. The owner of a house on the first row to the sea does not own the beach in front of it, and a hotel doesn’t become the owner of a beach simply because it is located in front of its building.

swim wherever you like

Signs saying “private beach,” “reserved for guests” or “no entry” do not automatically mean swimming is forbidden. If the beach is part of the maritime domain, then you are allowed to be there. A hotel, restaurant or concessionaire may charge for sunbeds, umbrellas, drinks, food or other services. However, they cannot charge you simply for being on the beach or entering the sea and swimming. You do not have to rent a sunbed, order a drink or be a hotel guest in order to swim there. You are free to bring your own towel, food, drinks and portable cooler.

sun loungers cannot occupy the entire beach

Empty sunbeds must not be used to reserve the beach. Just because someone rents out sunbeds does not mean they can occupy the whole beach in the morning and leave only a narrow path to the sea for other bathers. The same applies to towels left overnight – a towel does not reserve a spot for the next day. Anyone who wants a place on the beach has to come to the beach. Access to the shore may be restricted in military zones, special-purpose ports, shipyards, parts of harbours, or places where it is regulated for safety reasons.

there are exceptions with very special rules…

A very small number of beaches still operate under older concessions that allow special access rules. There are 15 such beaches in Croatia; better-known examples include Kostabela in Rijeka, Valalta in Rovinj and the beaches in front of Hotel Alan in Starigrad. These are exceptions. Under the 2023 Maritime Domain and Sea Ports Act, new sea beaches may not be fenced off, entrance fees may not be charged, and they may not be excluded from general public use except in strictly defined cases (for example, beaches belonging to public health institutions or designated nudist beaches).

the beach and the path leading to it are very different things

It is important to distinguish the beach itself from the path leading to it. The beach may be public, but the way to reach it can cross private land. If the only path to the beach goes through someone’s yard, garden, olive grove or fenced property, the owner can refuse you passage if there is no public path or right of way. The fact that it is the shortest or only land route does not give you the right to cross private property. In such cases you can reach the beach from the sea – by boat, kayak, SUP or by swimming. Once you have arrived legally, the owner of the house by the sea cannot forbid you from staying on the beach itself.

what if someone tries to kick you off a beach?

Don’t get into an argument. Ask on what basis they are forbidding you to stay. Photograph the sign, fence, padlock or the situation on the ground. If someone threatens you or tries to remove you physically, call the police on 192. If someone is fencing off the shore, locking access to the sea or illegally occupying a beach, you can report it to the harbour master’s office, municipal wardens or maritime inspectors.

The bottom line is simple: in Croatia, a beach in front of a hotel, campsite, restaurant or private villa is, as a rule, not private. You may swim, sunbathe and stay there. Just don’t try to reach it by cutting through someone else’s private garden.

World.title: The 3,500-Year-Old Sunken Settlement Near Zadar You Can Swim to
World.content:
August the 2nd, 2026 – There’s an absolutely fascinating 3,500-year-old sunken settlement not far from Zadar that you can swim to and explore yourself.

Hidden beneath the waters near Zadar lies an incredible archaeological discovery, an interesting prehistoric settlement dating back around 3,500 years that can be reached by swimming from the coast. Putni kofer writes that this ancient submerged site is located near the small island of Ričul, close to Turanj and near Galešnjak, the famous heart-shaped “Island of Love.” The remains lie in the Pašman Channel, only around 50 metres from the shore, at a depth of just two to three metres.

Although it is often described as a “sunken city”, archaeologists explain that it is actually a prehistoric settlement and harbour from way back during the Middle Bronze Age, a period about which relatively little was previously known in northern Dalmatia. The discovery revealed the remains of a large prehistoric harbour structure, including a stone embankment around 300 metres long that once connected the mainland area, known as Tukljača, with the island of Ričul.

Archaeologists also discovered thousands of artefacts, including fragments of pottery, tools, animal bones, wooden objects, and fishing equipment. One of the most remarkable finds was an olive stone believed to be the oldest discovered on the eastern Adriatic coast.

Researchers believe this settlement played an important role in protecting and controlling maritime routes along the eastern Adriatic coast. Its location made it strategically valuable for people who lived and travelled by sea thousands of years ago. The settlement belonged to a population that lived in the area before the emergence of the Liburnians, the ancient people who later became known as skilled sailors and traders of the Adriatic.

Today, the underwater archaeological site near Ričul offers a rare glimpse into prehistoric life on the Croatian coast. With the remains lying so close to shore and in shallow water, it is one of the most fascinating examples of Croatia’s very rich, hidden underwater heritage.

World.title: The Slavonian Banovac: The Croatian Town That Had Its Own Money
World.content:
August the 2nd, 2026 – Few have heard of the Slavonian banovac, but there’s a small, totally overlooked Croatian town that had its very own money over 770 years ago.

Long before Croatia existed as we know it today, and long before it had the kuna or the adopted the euro, a small town in Slavonia was already making history with its own currency. Turning the clock all the way back to the 13th century, the town of Pakrac was home to one of the first Croatian mints, where the famous Slavonian banovac was produced. Putni kofer writes that over 770 years later, this special medieval silver coin remains one of the most fascinating reminders of the town’s importance in Croatian history.

The first reliable written mention of Pakrac dates back to 1256, in a charter issued by King Béla IV. The same document mentions a mint located in the town, one of the earliest known mints in Croatia. Between 1256 and 1260, silver Slavonian banovacs were minted in Pakrac before the mint was later moved to Zagreb. These coins were known for their quality and widespread use, becoming an important medieval currency in the region.

The coin itself carried symbols that are still remembered today. One side featured a running marten, while the other showed a double cross with two crowned heads. The image of the marten later became connected with Croatian monetary tradition.

At the time, Pakrac was not just a small settlement. It was an important medieval centre with a powerful fortress, connected to the Knights Hospitaller, one of the influential military orders of the Middle Ages. Today, visitors can discover the story of the Slavonian banovac at the Museum of the City of Pakrac and learn about the town’s unusual role in Croatian financial history. The medieval coin has also inspired modern events celebrating Pakrac’s heritage, including the annual Slavonian Banovac fair.

A small Slavonian town once minted its own money, and over seven long centuries later, its medieval coin remains a symbol of Croatia’s exceptionally varied and rich history.

World.title: Croatia Among 22 EU Countries Calling for Urgent Response to Spanish Migrant Crisis
World.content:
August the 2nd, 2026 – Croatia is among 22 EU countries loudly calling for an urgent response and a meeting of EU interior ministers in response to the recent massive Spanish migrant crisis.

Index reports that Croatia is among 22 European Union countries calling for an urgent response from EU institutions following the migration crisis in Ceuta, a Spanish enclave in North Africa. The leaders of the 22 member states have sent a letter to the leadership of the European Union requesting an emergency video conference of interior ministers to discuss the situation and possible measures.

The request was initiated by Italy and Denmark, with the countries expressing concern over recent developments at the EU’s external border. They are calling for a coordinated European response to illegal migration and stronger protection of the Union’s external borders.

Among the countries that signed the letter is Croatia, which joined other EU members in asking for an urgent response to the Spanish migrant crisis. Croatia also wants to discuss how the EU responds to other migration challenges affecting European borders. The countries also warned about what they describe as the possible misuse of the asylum system and called for further action to prevent the instrumentalisation of migration.

The requested meeting would allow EU interior ministers to assess the situation in Ceuta and discuss measures to support Spain and strengthen cooperation between member states. The 22 countries are jointly stating that migration management requires a common European approach and that the protection of the EU’s external borders remains a shared responsibility.

World.title: Croatia Airlines Nears One Million Passengers Despite Huge Losses
World.content:
August the 2nd, 2025 – Croatia Airlines has managed to get close to one million passengers transported in the first half of 2026, despite enormous, continuous losses totalling almost 50 million euros.

Croatia Airlines carried a record 981,482 passengers during the first six months of 2026, the highest first-half passenger total in the company’s history, but the airline still posted a net loss of 49.7 million euros as rising operating costs and its fleet renewal programme continued to weigh on its finances.

Financial Findings reports that passenger numbers increased by 15% compared with the same period last year, with around 130,000 more travellers choosing the national carrier. The strongest growth came on international scheduled routes, where passenger numbers rose 18%, while domestic scheduled services recorded 6% growth. Overall, Croatia Airlines operated 12,631 flights during the first half of the year, a 2% increase year-on-year, while flight hours climbed 5% to 17,648 hours. The airline’s average passenger load factor also improved to 66.2%, up 2.7 percentage points from a year earlier.

The results outpaced growth across Croatia’s airport network as a whole. While passenger traffic at Croatian airports increased by around 3% to 5.5 million passengers during the first six months of the year, Croatia Airlines expanded five times faster, strengthening its market position.

Revenue also continued to rise. Operating revenue increased by 12%, with passenger transport accounting for 84% of total operating income. Passenger transport revenue alone was up 11% compared with the first half of 2025.

However, the higher income was offset by rapidly rising costs. Operating expenses increased 22%, producing an operating loss of 36.8 million euros, while the company’s overall net loss reached 49.7 million euros for the first half of 2026.

Croatia Airlines said several factors contributed to the weaker financial result. Fuel costs rose by 11.9 million euros, maintenance expenses increased by 4.9 million euros, and aviation service costs were up 3.4 million euros. The airline also incurred additional costs associated with introducing its new Airbus A220 fleet, including pilot and cabin crew training, operational adjustments and the temporary expense of operating multiple aircraft types simultaneously during the transition.

Fleet renewal remains the company’s biggest strategic investment. Two additional Airbus A220 aircraft joined the fleet during the first half of the year, bringing the total to nine. Croatia Airlines expects to receive another seven aircraft before the end of 2026, meaning 14 of the 15 ordered A220s should be in service by year-end. The carrier says replacing its older fleet with a single aircraft type will reduce maintenance and fuel costs, improve operational efficiency and enhance the passenger experience over the long term.

The airline also cited broader industry pressures, including geopolitical uncertainty, fuel price volatility, exchange-rate movements and continuing supply-chain disruptions affecting aircraft parts and maintenance services, all of which continue to impact airline operations across Europe.

World.title: Iraq offers discounts on Basrah crude during August
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) has offered considerable discounts on Basrah crude during August to attract customers to load shipments from within the Strait of Hormuz, according to a document reviewed by Reuters.

SOMO asked potential term purchasers to designate contractual volumes of Basrah Medium or Basrah Heavy crude for complimentary onboard delivery from the Basrah Oil Terminal or other port-related infrastructure.

SOMO provided discounts ranging between $25 and $27 per barrel on Basrah Medium, according to the loading period. It provided discounts of $27.80 to $29.80 a barrel for Basrah Heavy.

According to shipping statistics released on Monday, maritime activity in the strategic waterway of the Strait of Hormuz has slowed over the weekend due to reports of assaults on vessels.

Maritime traffic in the strait decreased due to ongoing military operations in the region and heightened shipping security risks.

The significant price reduction aims to compensate for rising maritime insurance costs and freight expenses by transferring transit risk to purchasers.

World.title: US forces gradually withdraw from northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – US forces have begun a phased withdrawal from Iraqi Kurdistan as part of a plan to redeploy and end their military presence in the country.

Reports indicate that US military convoys have left the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil, in the past few days, heading towards neighboring countries.

The withdrawal is being carried out in successive phases according to a set timetable, while the transfer of equipment and troops from US bases in the region continues.

The US Department of War has not yet issued an official statement regarding the details of these recent movements.

Reports also mentioned that the United States has begun withdrawing its remaining forces from Iraq ahead of the September 30 deadline, with Patriot air defense systems already removed from Erbil.

The pullout comes as regional security concerns rise, with Iranian-backed armed groups continuing to threaten the Kurdistan Region. These assaults have generated fears that reducing the United States’ military presence may make the region more vulnerable to security challenges.

The withdrawal is part of understandings reached between Baghdad and Washington over the past two years to end the mission of the US-led international coalition and transition to a new phase based on bilateral security and military cooperation.

Despite reducing its military presence, the United States has repeatedly affirmed its commitment to continued cooperation with Iraqi forces in training, intelligence sharing, and countering ISIS within a bilateral framework that does not require a large-scale military presence.

The withdrawal begins at a time when tensions in the region have risen in the past few weeks, following military operations by the US and Iran, as well as frequent drone and missile attacks on Iraqi Kurdistan.

World.title: Iraq, Iran discuss developments in the Strait of Hormuz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein and his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Aragchi, discussed on Sunday the latest developments in the Strait of Hormuz and prospects for regional de-escalation.

In a phone conversation, the two sides evaluated the most recent developments in the Strait of Hormuz during the last two days, as well as the implications for maritime security and regional stability, according to a statement released by the Iraqi Foreign Ministry.

Hussein emphasized Iraq’s support of dialogue and diplomacy as effective approaches to address disagreements and settle unresolved concerns, thereby helping to improve security and stability in the region.

The discussion also addressed the recent military assaults targeting Iraq and the significance of avoiding any actions that may escalate tensions in the region.

Aragchi reviewed the most recent developments and briefed Hussein on ongoing efforts to reach an agreement that would help reopen the Strait of Hormuz and ensure the smooth flow of maritime navigation.

Iraq is closely monitoring ongoing developments and expects to reach agreements that will facilitate the reopening of the Strait as soon as possible. This effort aims to ensure the security and stability of both the region and the global economy, according to Hussein.

Given the rapidly changing situation, Hussein emphasized the necessity of ongoing coordination between the two parties, as well as his support for steps taken to enhance dialogue.

World.title: Three drones target northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Three drones targeted the cities of Sulaimaniyah and Erbil in the Kurdistan region of Iraq early on Sunday before they were shot down without causing any casualties.

According to reports, two drones entered the skies over Sulaimaniyah. One of the two drones resulted in a fire that was eventually extinguished.

In Erbil, the C-RAM air defense system destroyed a drone early this morning without causing any damage.

These strikes follow the unexpected 72-hour pullout of US, British, French, and German forces from Erbil International Airport, which included hundreds of troops and heavy air defense equipment.

US forces have begun a phased withdrawal from Iraqi Kurdistan as part of a plan to redeploy and end their military presence in the country.

Reports indicate that US military convoys have departed from Erbil in the past few days, heading toward neighboring countries.

The US Department of War has not yet issued an official statement regarding the details of these recent movements.

The international coalition’s air defense systems in Erbil intercepted several earlier drones targeting the US consulate and its associated logistics base.

The recent escalation in Iraqi Kurdistan, which largely included drone assaults over Erbil, comes amid rising tensions between the United States and Iran, the most serious since a cease-fire deal was reached in mid-June.

World.title: Iraq forms security committee to prevent attacks against neighboring states
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, Ali al-Zaidi, chaired an emergency meeting on Saturday to discuss security developments in the region.

Al-Zaidi emphasized the need to prevent any violation or threat emerging from Iraqi land toward neighboring nations, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister directed the establishment of a joint security committee to address current challenges and to follow deterrent procedures to prevent attacks or potential violations against neighboring countries.

Al-Zaidi also directed Iraqi security forces to enhance stability, protect sovereignty, and maintain good neighborly relations.

The meeting addressed the Iraqi army’s readiness to counter any attempt to strike neighboring nations, as well as Iraq’s unwavering commitment to prevent the use of its territory to launch attacks against other countries.

The formation of a joint security committee is part of Iraq’s responsibility to preserve national sovereignty and uphold the principles of good neighborliness and international law.

The decision to form this committee follows substantial regional triggering events in recent days.

The United States and Saudi Arabia launched coordinated attacks on targets in several Iraqi provinces. The alliance declared that these were retaliation strikes in response to drone and missile assaults on regional oil infrastructure and military targets.

Prior to the security meeting, Jordan and Syria cautioned Baghdad about Iran-backed armed groups operating in Iraq, warning that cross-border threats would not go unnoticed.

World.title: Iraqi court recovers IQD 20 billion in corruption and money laundering cases
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s Rusafa Investigative Court, which specializes in integrity and money laundering cases, has recovered 20 billion Iraqi dinars (approximately $15.3 million) linked to financial corruption, administrative misconduct, and fraud, the country’s judiciary announced on Sunday.

In a statement, the judiciary’s media office said the recovered funds were tied to investigations involving financial and administrative corruption as well as financial fraud.

The court said the recovery forms part of ongoing legal efforts to pursue individuals accused of using illegal methods to obtain profits at the expense of public funds.

Authorities stressed that legal proceedings against those involved remain underway, reaffirming their commitment to combating corruption and protecting state resources.

The judiciary did not disclose additional details regarding the individuals or entities involved, nor did it specify when the alleged offenses occurred.

World.title: US Embassy in Iraq urges Americans to leave the Middle East
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The US Embassy in Baghdad and the US Consulate General in Erbil advised American citizens on Saturday to leave the Middle East as tensions in the region remained high.

The US mission said in a statement that due to heightened tensions in the Middle East, the security environment remains complex with the potential for unforeseen escalation.

The mission added that Americans presently in the Middle East should exercise extreme caution and alertness and be prepared for flight cancellations, frequent airspace closures, and possible travel difficulties.

Some regional airlines have postponed the restart of previously scheduled flights, while others have cancelled some routes.

Americans in the region are advised to consider departing or to be ready to leave if tensions escalate.

In a statement, the US Embassy in Baghdad advised that those who choose to travel to or from the region should closely monitor updates regarding airport and airline operations.

US diplomatic installations, especially those outside the Middle East, have been attacked. Iran and pro-Iran groups may attack additional US interests abroad or at areas connected with the US and Americans across the world, such as US corporations and institutions, according to the statement.

The Iranian leadership is unpredictable, as seen by recent moves to strike regions without notice, as well as to expand assaults to previously untargeted territories such as Egypt, according to the US Embassy in Iraq.

The US Embassy advised Americans to remain vigilant, as the absence of past attacks on US interests or businesses in a country does not ensure their safety.

World.title: Iraq, NATO agree to open mission office in Baghdad, expand security cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews,com) — Iraqi National Security Adviser Qasim al-Aboudi and the commander of the NATO Mission Iraq (NMI), Lt. Gen. Ramon Armada, agreed on Sunday to open a NATO mission office in Baghdad while reaffirming continued cooperation on military training, cybersecurity, and strategic security partnerships.

According to a statement from al-Aboudi’s media office, cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), the two officials held talks via video conference to discuss regional security developments and NATO’s ongoing support for Iraq’s armed forces.

During the discussion, both sides stressed the importance of reducing regional tensions and resolving recurring crises through dialogue and diplomatic channels. They also reviewed mechanisms for continuing NATO assistance in the areas of military training, advisory support, intelligence sharing, and capacity building.

A key outcome of the meeting was an agreement to establish a NATO Mission office in Baghdad, further strengthening coordination between the alliance and Iraqi security institutions.

Al-Aboudi said NATO’s role in Iraq remains focused on non-combat activities, including military advisory services, training, capacity building, cybersecurity support, and cooperation in artificial intelligence. He added that Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government is pursuing a policy of engagement with friendly and neighboring countries to advance development, investment, and mutually beneficial partnerships.

For his part, Armada reaffirmed that NATO’s advisory and training mission is committed to helping develop the capabilities of Iraq’s armed forces to address future security challenges. He said the alliance remains committed to supporting Iraq in line with the priorities established by the Iraqi government.

World.title: ‘Non-cooperation by state’: SC raps Arunachal Pradesh govt, summons top officials in CBI probe involving CM Khandu’s kin
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday summoned Arunachal Pradesh chief secretary and principal secretary (home) over what it termed the state governmentâs ânon-cooperationâ in a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)

involving family members of chief minister Pema Khandu.

After perusing the CBIâs status report in the case, a bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta directed both officers to appear before it on August 24 along with their responses to the report and explain the alleged non-cooperation.

âWe have perused the status report given by the CBI dated July 17. A perusal of the same reflects that there is non-cooperation on the part of the state government in providing the necessary records,â the bench said, according to PTI.

The observation came after Additional Solicitor General (ASG) KM Nataraj, appearing for the CBI, informed the Supreme Court that the probe agency had sought more time to complete the enquiry and that Arunachal Pradesh authorities were not cooperating with the investigation.

âWe will call the chief secretary,â the bench observed, while questioning the CBI on why it had given a âlong ropeâ despite the alleged non-cooperation.





âWhy do you need anything more for registering an RC (regular case)?â the judges asked ASG Nataraj.

âBoth the aforesaid officers shall remain present before this court along with their responses to the CBIâs report and also explain why there is non-cooperation and non-compliance with the order of this court,â the bench stated, while posting the matter for hearing on August 24.

World.title: Karnataka expands cabinet, 20 netas take oath; DKS hits back on ministerial berth row
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Twenty new ministers were inducted into the Karnataka government on Monday as chief minister

expanded his Cabinet to its full strength, two months after taking office.

The swearing-in ceremony took place at Lok Bhavan in Bengaluru after Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot approved the expansion.

The Cabinet expansion increased the strength of the ministry to the sanctioned limit of 34, including the chief minister.

Among those sworn in were PM Narendraswamy, Shivaraj Tangadagi, Rudrappa Lamani, KS Basavanthappa, B Nagendra, T Raghumoorthy, BZ Zameer Ahmed Khan, Rizwan Arshad, Santosh Lad, Madhu Bangarappa, Putturangashetty, SS Mallikarjun, Dr Ajay Singh, N Chaluvaraya Swamy, KM Shivalinge Gowda, HC Balakrishna, Gayathri Shanthegowda, Basavaraj Rayareddi, Vijayanand Kashappanavar and Laxman Savadi.

The Congress high command also approved GS Patil as the new Speaker of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly and AS Ponnanna as the Deputy Speaker. Saleem Ahmed was named Chairman of the Legislative Council, while Umashree was appointed Deputy Chairperson.

Ahead of the ceremony, Congress MLAs Yashavantarayagouda V Patil (Indi) and Belur Gopalakrishna (Sagar) resigned from the Karnataka Legislative assembly after being left out of the Cabinet.





Patil claimed his name had been included in the list until Monday morning but was removed from the final list released by the party.

"I was promised a ministerial post even before the 2023 Assembly polls. Later, I was told it would happen after 2.5 years, but the promise was not kept. I have no other choice," he said.

He added that he was not resigning from the Congress but felt compelled to step down as MLA, calling it an insult to the people of his constituency.

His supporters also staged a protest in Bengaluru over his exclusion.

Reacting to the disappointment among party legislators, Shivakumar urged them to remain patient.

"There are many MLAs. It is not possible to accommodate everyone. Earlier, I too missed out on a ministerial berth in Siddaramaiah's Cabinet. But didn't I become a minister later? Similarly, we will provide opportunities to everyone in the future," the chief minister said.

He also said, "I request them to be patient. We will create opportunities for everyone."

The expansion saw the return of several former ministers, including B Nagendra, who had resigned from the previous Siddaramaiah government in 2024 over allegations linked to the Karnataka Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation scam.

Gayathri Shanthegowda is the only woman inducted in the expanded ministry. Three children of former chief ministers are now part of the Cabinet: Yathindra Siddaramaiah, Madhu Bangarappa and Dr Ajay Singh.

World.title: Pregnancy found growing near kidneys in rare medical case
World.content:
An extremely rare pregnancy that developed outside the uterus, deep inside the abdomen near the kidneys (Representative image)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Doctors in Delhi have successfully treated a woman diagnosed with an extremely rare pregnancy that developed outside the uterus, deep inside the abdomen near the kidneys, using minimally invasive (keyhole) surgery.The woman, from Bengaluru, had initially presented for a routine pregnancy evaluation. During an ultrasound, doctors detected a 10-12 cm cystic structure, which was initially suspected to be a dermoid cyst because it appeared to contain fetal parts. However, an MRI revealed a far more unusual diagnosis.The scan showed uterine dehiscence, in which the uterine wall had ruptured, allowing the pregnancy to develop in the retroperitoneal space, close to the kidneys and major blood vessels, including the aorta and inferior vena cava. Doctors found a 12-week fetus measuring about 7-8 cm inside the cyst.Dr Mannan Gupta, Founder and Chairman, Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Elantis Healthcare, said the pregnancy was neither inside the uterus nor in the fallopian tube or ovary, where most ectopic pregnancies occur."Initially, the ultrasound findings suggested a dermoid cyst. However, MRI revealed an exceptionally rare condition. The pregnancy was located in the retroperitoneal space near the kidneys and major blood vessels.This is one of the rarest forms of pregnancy and the first such case I have encountered in my career," he said.Doctors performed the procedure laparoscopically, avoiding a major abdominal incision. Given the proximity of the pregnancy to vital organs and major blood vessels, the surgery required meticulous planning and precision. Doctors said the patient had an excellent postoperative outcome.According to the treating doctors, retroperitoneal pregnancy is estimated to occur in about one in 30,000 pregnancies. They said early diagnosis and timely intervention are critical, as delayed treatment can result in life-threatening complications because of the pregnancy's proximity to major blood vessels and vital organs.

World.title: ‘Can some amount be released from frozen TMC funds?’ SC asks ED on Mamata-led faction’s plea
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

on Monday asked the

(ED) whether a portion of the funds from the frozen bank accounts of the Mamata Banerjee-led faction of the

(TMC) could be released to meet the partyâs day-to-day expenses through a Calcutta high court-appointed special officer.

Additional Solicitor General (ASG) SV Raju, appearing for the central probe agency, told a bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale that he would seek instructions on the matter.

The bench subsequently posted the matter for hearing on August 11.

During the hearing, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for the Banerjee-led faction, which is the petitioner in the case, argued that the party was unable to even pay salaries to its employees due to the freezing of its accounts.

The top court is hearing a plea filed by the Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool faction challenging the July 20 order of the Calcutta high court.

The high court had refused to grant interim relief to the group to operate three TMC bank accounts that had been frozen by the ED.

Referring to the high courtâs order, Sibal said, âWhat does the impugned order say? It says there are 36 separate accounts which are not seized. That is factually incorrect.â





Raju opposed the submissions and informed the bench that an investigation was underway. The ASG also alleged that money laundering had taken place through those accounts.

The anti-money laundering law âis not only for actual money laundering but also for prevention of money laundering. We are preventing it,â the ASG added.

When Raju claimed there was a âcontinuous offenceâ, Sibal countered the submission and questioned how such an argument could be made when the bank accounts had already been frozen.

The bench was informed that the high court had appointed a former Calcutta high court judge as a special officer to oversee the operation of the three bank accounts for meeting the day-to-day expenses of running the political party.

It was during this discussion that the Supreme Court suggested whether some amount could be released in favour of the special officer to meet the partyâs daily expenses.

The ED froze the three bank accounts, with a combined balance of Rs 440.42 crore, as part of its money laundering probe stemming from an FIR registered by the West Bengal Police over alleged dishonest financial transactions, unlawful collection of funds and routing of suspected money through certain party accounts.

In its order, the high court had noted that apart from the three accounts placed under a âdebit-freezeâ by the ED, there were 36 other accounts in the partyâs name, with around Rs 164 crore lying in them.

Subsequently, the Mamata Banerjee-led faction of the TMC approached the high court challenging the initiation of ECIR (Enforcement Case Information Report) proceedings by the ED, which is equivalent to an FIR.

World.title: 'People become Leftist after meeting Islamists': Kangana Ranaut says she's now an 'awakened Hindu'
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

and actor

on Monday claimed that 'people become Leftist after meeting Islamists' in a new social media video posted on X. The Mandi MP also spoke about her ideological journey, saying she was a 'moderate Hindu' and now wants to be an 'awakened Hindu'.

The clip comes days after Ranaut sparked controversy by describing Gen Z protesters involved in the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP)-led agitation over the alleged NEET paper leak as 'generation gutter'.

In the video message, Ranaut said she wanted to share her thoughts before leaving for Parliament.

"Even though I am getting late for the Parliament, I thought I would share my feelings with you," she said.

Referring to women in the film industry, Ranaut said many Hindu women she had met did not have a clear political or religious ideology.

"We have seen and known many Hindu daughters and sisters in the film industry... They may be Hindu, but they have no ideology about politics or religion. This is usually the case in youth. They are very neutral," she said.

She then claimed that people's thinking changes after coming into contact with "Islamists".

"But as soon as they are in contact with Islamists, their thinking becomes so defined that they become Leftist.





I think there is no harm in that because the Constitution gives you freedom. You can adopt any religion or ideology you want," Ranaut said.

Speaking about herself, the BJP MP said she no longer considered herself a 'moderate Hindu'.

"But when it comes to Hindu daughters, I will not defend myself... Yes, I was a moderate Hindu," she said.

"Today, I am being harassed. Since when did you become a Sanghi? I want to become a Sanghi.

I want to become an awakened Hindu like BJP and RSS. I want to convert. Why can't I convert?" she added.

Ranaut also argued that Hindu women should have the freedom to adopt a defined ideological identity.

"I used to do everything. But today, I also want to convert. I want to become a defined and awakened Hindu. Why is that path closed for me? This double-minded thinking will not work," she said.

The remarks come amid an ongoing war of words between Ranaut and Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders after she criticised young protesters and referred to them as "generation gutter" following the CJP-led protests over the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak.

CJP leaders had responded by saying her remarks were not taken seriously, even within her own party.

World.title: 'Will emperor show his degree?' Abhijeet Dipke says he's ready to reveal scholarship, loan records
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Monday challenged BJP leaders to make their educational qualifications public after an RTI query was filed seeking details of the funding for his studies abroad.

In a video message shared on social media, Dipke said he was ready to disclose all documents related to his education.

"I just saw that a BJP worker has filed an RTI against me. I want to ask them: will your leaders show their degrees? I am ready to show my scholarship documents and my educational records," he said.

In a post on X, Dipke also wrote, "I am ready to reveal my scholarship letter & education loan letter. Will the emperor show his degree?"

His remarks came after a Surat-based RTI activist sought an inquiry into the finances of Dipke's father, a retired Maharashtra government employee, questioning how he funded his son's education in the United States.

Speaking to PTI, Dipke said there was nothing to hide and maintained that his education was funded through a scholarship and an education loan.

"Those who wish to investigate my education funding are free to do so," he said.

Dipke said he received a scholarship from Boston University and financed the remaining expenses through an education loan, which he is still repaying.

"I received a scholarship from Boston University, and for the remaining amount, I took an education loan.





It is still pending and has to be repaid. The fight is not personal," he said.

The 30-year-old, who holds a Master of Science degree in Public Relations from Boston University, returned to India in June and led the Cockroach Janta Party's agitation over the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak. The protests eventually led to the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as education minister.

Dipke also dismissed attempts to link the CJP protests with political movements in neighbouring countries.

"Protests in Bangladesh, Nepal are being used to defame us; we are different," he said.

He expressed hope that the Maharashtra government would withdraw police cases against students who participated in the protests.

"Maharashtra has always led the nation through its progressive legacy. I hope the state government will not harass any student. They have done nothing wrong â they were only fighting for their future," he said.

He also urged authorities to examine whether the organisation should be registered as a political party under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.

World.title: Lok Sabha clears bill to increase number of Supreme Court judges, without debate
World.content:
The bill proposes to increase the number of Supreme Court judges from the present 33 to 37, excluding the CJI
